<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Environment Act <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25" id="c00015" Year="1995" Number="25" Class="UnitedKingdomPublicGeneralAct">1995 (c.25)</Citation> is amended as follows.</Text>

<P2para>

<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/2/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/2/a" id="section-24-2-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>

<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/2/a/i" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/2/a/i" id="section-24-2-a-i">

<BlockAmendment Context="main" PartialRefs="p10001" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">

<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>

</P4para>
</P4>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>;</AppendText>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/2/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/2/b" id="section-24-2-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>

<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<P2>
<Pnumber>2B</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In subsection (2)(o)(ii), “stationary idling offence means an offence under section 42 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 that consists of a contravention of, or failure to comply with, so much of regulation 98 of the Road Vehicle (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986 (stopping of engine when stationary) as relates to the prevention of exhaust emissions.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/3" id="section-24-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In Schedule 11 (air quality: supplemental provision), in paragraph 5 (fixed penalty offences), in sub-paragraph (6)—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/a" id="section-24-3-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>

<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/a/i" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/a/i" id="section-24-3-a-i">
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>the words from “a penalty of such amount” to the end become paragraph (a);</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/a/ii" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/a/ii" id="section-24-3-a-ii">
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>at the end of paragraph (a) insert </Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="schedule" PartialRefs="p10002" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<Text>, or</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>a penalty of such amount falling within a range prescribed in regulations as is specified in a fixed penalty notice;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>;</AppendText>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2/section/24/3/b" id="section-24-3-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>

</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Pblock></Chapter></Part></Body></Primary></Legislation>

<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After section 6A of the Environment Act (as inserted by section 39 of this Act), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<Pblock>
<Title>Biodiversity targets</Title>
<P1group>
<Title>Biodiversity targets: general</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6B</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers may by regulations set targets in respect of any matter relating to biodiversity in Wales.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers may set a target in the regulations only if they are satisfied that meeting it would contribute to halting and reversing the decline in biodiversity or to restoring biodiversity to resilient levels, in particular through one or more of the following—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>increasing the abundance of native species;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>enhancing the resilience of ecosystems (in particular the aspects specified in section 6(2)(a) to (e));</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>increasing genetic diversity.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In considering whether a target would contribute to‍ the matters specified in subsection (2)(a), (b) or (c), the Welsh Ministers must have regard to the list published under section 7.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The regulations must, in relation to each target—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>specify a standard to be achieved, which must be capable of being objectively measured, and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>specify a date by which the standard is to be achieved.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The regulations must—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>include provision about how to measure—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>progress towards achieving each standard specified under subsection (4), and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>whether the standard has been achieved, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>specify indicators as a means of measuring those things.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A target under this section is set when the regulations setting it come into force.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In this section—</Text>
<OrderedList Type="alpha" Decoration="parens">
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>“<Term>native species</Term>” means species that naturally occur or have in the past naturally occurred in Wales, including—</Text>
<OrderedList Type="roman" Decoration="parens">
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>regularly occurring migratory species (both breeding and non-breeding) and natural colonists, and</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>species that have been reintroduced in Wales following past extinction;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>“<Term>natural colonists</Term>” means species that arrived in Wales of their own accord and have become established, including those that become migratory species.</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>8</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In sections 6C, 6D, 6G, 6H and 6I, “specified standard” and “<Term>specified date</Term>”, in relation to a target set under this section, mean the standard and date specified under subsection (4).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Duty to make regulations setting targets: priority areas</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6C</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must exercise the power in section 6B to‍ —</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>set a long-term target in respect of at least one matter within each of the priority areas in subsection (2)(a) and (b),</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>set a short-term target in respect of at least one matter within each of the priority areas in subsection (2)(a) and (b), and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>set a target in respect of at least one matter within each of the priority areas in subsection (2)(c) and (d).</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The priority areas are—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>reducing the risk of the extinction of native species;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the effective management of ecosystems;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>reducing pollution;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the quality of evidence to inform decisions relating to biodiversity, access to that evidence and its use and application.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A target is a “long-term target” if the specified date is at least 15 years after the date on which the target is set.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A target is a “short-term target” if the specified date is less than 15 years after the date on which the target is set.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Targets may not be set in respect of a matter within the priority area in subsection (2)(c) if a target may be set in respect of that matter under the Environment (Air Quality and Soundscapes) (Wales) Act <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2024/2" id="c00014" Year="2024" Number="2" Class="WelshParliamentAct">2024 (asc 2)</Citation>.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In subsection (2)(a), ”native species” has the meaning given by section 6B(7).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must lay a draft of a Welsh statutory instrument containing the regulations required by this section before Senedd Cymru before the end of the period of‍ 2 years beginning with the date on which the Environment (Principles, Governance and Biodiversity Targets) (Wales) Act 2026 (asc xx) receives Royal Assent.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Target-setting process</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6D</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Before making regulations under section 6B, the Welsh Ministers must seek advice from persons they consider to be independent and to have relevant expertise.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must publish a summary of any such advice they receive.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>When making regulations under section 6B, the Welsh Ministers must apply the principles of sustainable management of natural resources.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Before making regulations under section 6B, the Welsh Ministers must publish a report summarising—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the consultation that was carried out in connection with the regulations, and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>any representations that were received as a result of the consultation.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Before making regulations under section 6B that set or amend a target, the Welsh Ministers must be satisfied that the target or amended target can be met.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>For the purposes of this Part, a target is met if the specified standard is achieved by the specified date.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Subsections (1) to‍ (4) do not apply to provisions in regulations under section 6B that revoke a target that has been met.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Duty to meet targets</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6E</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must ensure that targets set in regulations made under section 6B are met.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Designation of public authorities for the purpose of section 6(2A)</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6F</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers may by regulations designate a public authority within section 6(11) in relation to a target set in regulations made under section 6B.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Before making regulations under this section, the Welsh Ministers must consult—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the public authority they propose to designate, and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>such other persons as they consider appropriate.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Review of targets</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6G</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers may, from time to time, review a target set in regulations under section 6B.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must review a target set in regulations under section 6B if it appears to them—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>that the target may not be met, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>that the target may no longer be appropriate.‍</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers may, from time to time, review the effectiveness of all current targets for the purpose of determining whether setting further targets in regulations under section 6B would be more effective in contributing to halting and reversing the decline in biodiversity or to restoring biodiversity to resilient levels.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must review the effectiveness of all current targets for the purpose mentioned in subsection (3)—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>if a target set in regulations under section 6B has not been met by the specified date in relation to that target;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>if 10 years have passed since the most recently completed review under any of subsection (3), this subsection or subsection (5).</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>If no review under subsection (3) or (4) has been completed before the end of 2041, the Welsh Ministers must review the effectiveness of all current targets for the purpose mentioned in subsection (3).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A target is current for the purpose of subsections (3) to (5) if—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>it has been set in regulations under section 6B that are in force at the time of the review, and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>it has not been met at that time.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In carrying out a review under this section, the Welsh Ministers must seek advice from persons they consider to be independent and to have relevant expertise.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>8</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must publish a summary of any such advice they receive.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>9</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After carrying out a review under this section, the Welsh Ministers must lay before Senedd Cymru, and publish, a statement noting its conclusions.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>10</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>If‍ a review under subsection (1) or (2) concludes that a target will not be met or is no longer appropriate, the statement must note the reasons for that conclusion and the steps, if any, the Welsh Ministers intend to take in relation to the target in consequence of the review.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>11</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>If a review under subsection (3), (4) or (5) concludes that further targets should be set in regulations under section 6B, the Welsh Ministers must lay a draft of a Welsh statutory instrument containing such regulations before Senedd Cymru before the end of the period of 2 years beginning with the day on which the review was completed.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>12</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A review is completed for the purpose of subsections (4)(b), (5) and (11) when the statement required by subsection (9) is published.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Revoking or lowering targets</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6H</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers may not make regulations under section 6B that revoke or lower a target (the “existing target”) unless they are satisfied that—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>because of changes to the evidence to which they had regard when setting the existing target, meeting it would not contribute to halting and reversing the decline in biodiversity or to restoring biodiversity to resilient levels,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>meeting the existing target would have no significant benefit compared with not meeting it or with meeting a lower target,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>because of changes in circumstances since the existing target was set, the environmental, social, economic or other costs of meeting it would be disproportionate to the benefits, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>meeting the existing target is no longer achievable—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>because of changes in circumstances since the existing target was set, or</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>because of changes to the evidence to which the Welsh Ministers had regard when setting the existing target.</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>If the Welsh Ministers are satisfied that—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the costs of meeting the existing target would be disproportionate to the benefits as mentioned in subsection (1)(c), or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>meeting the existing target is no longer achievable as mentioned in subsection (1)(d),</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<Text>they must, before making regulations under section 6B that revoke the target, consider whether to make regulations that lower the target.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Before making regulations under section 6B that revoke or lower a target, the Welsh Ministers must lay before Senedd Cymru, and publish, a statement explaining why the Welsh Ministers are satisfied as mentioned in subsection (1).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Regulations lower a target if, to any extent, they—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>replace the specified standard with a lower standard, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>replace the specified date with a later date.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>This section does not apply to provisions in regulations under section 6B that revoke a target that has been met.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Statement about targets</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">6I</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>On or before the specified date in relation to each target set under regulations under section 6B, the Welsh Ministers must lay before Senedd Cymru, and publish, a statement containing the required information.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The required information is (as appropriate)—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>that the target has been met,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>that the target has not been met, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>that the Welsh Ministers are not yet able to determine whether the target has been met, the reasons for that and the steps the Welsh Ministers intend to take in order to determine whether the target has been met.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Where the Welsh Ministers make a statement that a target has not been met, the Welsh Ministers must, before the end of‍ 6 months beginning with the date on which the statement is laid, lay before Senedd Cymru, and publish, a report.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The report must—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>explain why the target has not been met, and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>set out the steps the Welsh Ministers have taken, or intend to take, to ensure the target is met as soon as reasonably practicable.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Before deciding on the steps referred to in subsection (4)(b), the Welsh Ministers must seek advice from persons they consider to be independent and to have relevant expertise.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Welsh Ministers must publish a summary of any such advice they receive.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Where the Welsh Ministers make a statement that they are not yet able to determine whether a target has been met, the Welsh Ministers must, before the end of 6 months beginning with the date on which the statement is laid, lay before Senedd Cymru, and publish, a further statement containing the required information.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>8</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Subsections (2) to (7) apply to further statements under subsection (7) as they apply to a statement under subsection (1).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
</Pblock>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/4/section/35/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/4/section/35/2" id="section-35-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Before section 7 of the Environment Act, insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<FragmentTitle Context="Pblock">
<Title>Biodiversity lists</Title>
</FragmentTitle>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/4/section/35/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/4/section/35/3" id="section-35-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In section 25(4) of the Environment Act, after “section 22(1)” insert <InlineAmendment>“, or to revoke a target that has been set in regulations under section 6B and that has been met,”</InlineAmendment>.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Part></Body></Primary></Legislation>

<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/4/section/38/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/4/section/38/1" id="section-38-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In section 6(7) of the Environment Act, for “to comply with subsection (1)” substitute</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" PartialRefs="p10001" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<Text id="p10001"> —</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>to comply with subsection (1), and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>where subsection (2A) applies, to contribute to meeting the target in relation to which it has been designated</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/4/section/38/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/4/section/38/2" id="section-38-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After section 6(7) of the Environment Act, insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<P2>
<Pnumber>7A</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The report published by the Welsh Ministers under subsection (7) must, in particular, report on the progress being made towards meeting the targets set in regulations under section 6B and whether they are likely to be met.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7B</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>As soon as reasonably practicable after publishing their report under subsection (7), the Welsh Ministers must send a copy of it to the Office of Environmental Governance Wales.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7C</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Sending a copy of the report under subsection (7B) is to be treated as a request by the Welsh Ministers to the Office of Environmental Governance Wales for advice under section 13 of the Environment (Principles, Governance and Biodiversity Targets) (Wales) Act 2026 (asc xx).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Part></Body></Primary></Legislation>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5" NumberOfProvisions="201" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="2.0" TerritorialApplication="W" RestrictExtent="E+W" RestrictStartDate="2026-04-28"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/body" NumberOfProvisions="156" NumberFormat="default" TerritorialApplication="W" RestrictExtent="E+W" RestrictStartDate="2026-04-28"><Part DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/part/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/part/5" NumberOfProvisions="25" id="part-5" TerritorialApplication="W" RestrictExtent="E+W" RestrictStartDate="2026-04-28"><Number>PART 5</Number><Title>SUPPLEMENTARY AND GENERAL</Title><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/part/5/crossheading/guidance-and-cooperation" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/part/5/crossheading/guidance-and-cooperation" NumberOfProvisions="5" id="part-5-crossheading-guidance-and-cooperation" TerritorialApplication="W" RestrictExtent="E+W" Match="false" Status="Prospective"><Title>Guidance and co-operation</Title><P1group Match="false" Status="Prospective" RestrictExtent="E+W" TerritorialApplication="W"><Title>Co-operation and information: duties of responsible persons under Fire Safety Order</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121" id="section-121">
<Pnumber PuncAfter=""><CommentaryRef Ref="key-14ca6f"/>121</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/1" id="section-121-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Fire Safety Order is amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/2" id="section-121-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After article 22B insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<P1group>
<Title>Wales: co-operation with accountable persons and duty holders</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">22C</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>This article applies in relation to premises forming part of a building where—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the building, or any part of it, is a regulated building, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>any part of the building is a relevant HMO.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The responsible person for the premises (“<Term>P</Term>”) must take such steps as are reasonably practicable to ascertain whether there are one or more other persons who are (as the case may be)—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>accountable persons for the regulated building, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>duty holders for the relevant HMO.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>If there are, P must co-operate with each of those persons for the purpose of those persons carrying out their duties under the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>If P becomes aware that a person is treated as an accountable person for the building by virtue of section 36 of the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026, P must co-operate with the person for the purpose of the person carrying out their duties under that Act.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>‍5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In this article, article 22D and article 22E—</Text>
<UnorderedList Class="Definition" Decoration="none">
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>“<Term>accountable person</Term>” has the meaning given by section 8 of the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>“<Term>duty holder</Term>” has the meaning given by section 79 of that Act;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>“<Term>regulated building</Term>” has the meaning given by sections 2 and 7 of that Act;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>“<Term>relevant HMO</Term>” has the meaning given by section 78 of that Act.</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Wales: sharing information with accountable person‍s</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">22D</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>This article applies in relation to premises forming part of a building where the building, or any part of it, is a regulated building.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A responsible person in relation to the premises must give information or a document to a person (“<Term>A</Term>”) who—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>is either—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>an accountable person for the building, or</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>a person treated as an accountable person for the building by virtue of section 36 of the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>makes a request in accordance with paragraph (3).</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A request is made in accordance with this paragraph if—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the information or document is necessary for A to comply with a requirement under the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026 or regulations made under it,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>A gives the relevant person a written request that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>states that the request is made pursuant to this article,</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>explains why A requires the information or document,</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>iii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>states the address to which the information or document must be given, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>iv</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>states that the information or document must be given before the end of a specified date no less than 14 days after the day on which the request is given, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>it is reasonable for the relevant person to give A the information or document.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The disclosure of information or a document in accordance with this section does not breach—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>any obligation of confidence owed by the person making the disclosure, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>any other restriction on the disclosure of information or a document (however imposed).</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>But see also section 183A of the Data Protection Act <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/2018/12" id="c00028" Year="2018" Number="12" Class="UnitedKingdomPublicGeneralAct">2018 (c. 12)</Citation> (protection of requirements for processing personal data).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
<P1group>
<Title>Wales: provision of information to duty holders</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">22E</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>This article applies in relation to premises forming part of a building where any part of the building is a relevant HMO.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A responsible person in relation to the premises must give information or a document to a person (“<Term>D</Term>”) who—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>is a duty holder for a relevant HMO in the building, and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>makes a request in accordance with paragraph (3).</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>A request is made in accordance with this paragraph if—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the information or document requested is necessary for D to comply with a requirement under the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026 or regulations made under it,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>D gives the responsible person a written request that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>states that the request is made pursuant to this article,</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>explains why D requires the information or document,</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>iii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>states the address to which the information or document must be given, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>iv</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>states that the information or document must be given before the end of a specified date no less than 14 days after the day on which the request is given, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>it is reasonable for the responsible person to give D the information or document.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The disclosure of information or a document in accordance with this section does not breach—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>any obligation of confidence owed by the person making the disclosure, or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>any other restriction on the disclosure of information or a document (however imposed).</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>But see also section 183A of the Data Protection Act <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/2018/12" id="c00029" Year="2018" Number="12" Class="UnitedKingdomPublicGeneralAct">2018 (c. 12)</Citation> (protection of requirements for processing personal data).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/3" id="section-121-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In the heading of article 22B, for “Co-operation” substitute <InlineAmendment>“England: co-operation”</InlineAmendment>.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/4" id="section-121-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In the following provisions, for “22B” substitute ‍“22E”—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/4/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/4/a" id="section-121-4-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>article 5(1), (2), (3) and (5);‍</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/4/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/4/b" id="section-121-4-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>article 50(1) and (1A).‍</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/5" id="section-121-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In article 26, after paragraph (3), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraph (1), the reference to “this Order does not include Articles 22C to 22E (but see section 94 of the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/6" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/6" id="section-121-6">
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In article 27, after paragraph (5), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraph (1), references to “this Order do not include Articles 22C to 22E.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/7" id="section-121-7">
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In article 30, after paragraph (7), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<P2>
<Pnumber>8</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraphs (1) and (4), references to “this Order do not include Articles 22C to 22E.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asc/2026/5/section/121/8" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asc/2026/5/section/121/8" id="section-121-8">
<Pnumber>8</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In article 36, after paragraph (6), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="default" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown">
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraph (1)(a), the reference to “this Order does not include Articles 22C to 22E.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Pblock></Part></Body></Primary></Legislation>

A1</Number><TitleBlock><Title>Water Industry Commission for Scotland(introduced by section 1(4))Status11The Commission is a body corporate.2The Commission—ais not a servant or agent of the Crown,bhas Scottish Ministers for such period as is specified in the appointment,bmay, by written notice to the Scottish Ministers, resign as a member,cin other respects, holds and vacates office on such terms and conditions as the Scottish Ministers may determine, anddafter ceasing to hold office is eligible for reappointment as a member.2The Scottish Ministers may remove an ordinary member from office and Commission, andbmay, after consulting that member, appoint another ordinary member to act as deputy to that member.2The member appointed to chair the meetings and any member appointed to act as deputy to that member hold and vacate office as such in accordance with the terms of their appointments.3A member so appointed may, by written notice to the Scottish Ministers, resign from office as such.4A member so appointed vacates office on ceasing to be a member of the Commission.5Where a member—ais appointed to chair meetings or to act as deputy to the member so appointed, orbceases to hold office Ministers may determine in respect of expenses properly incurred in the performance of their duties as a member.3Where a person ceases to be an ordinary member otherwise than on the expiry of that person's term of appointment, the Scottish Ministers may, if they think there are special circumstances, direct the Commission to pay to the person such amount of compensation as they may determine.4The Scottish Ministers may direct the Commission to pay—asuch pension, allowance or gratuity to, or in respect of, any person who is or has been an ordinary member,bsuch contribution or other payment towards provision for such pension, allowance or gratuity,as they consider appropriate.Chief executive71The Commission is to employ a chief executive.2The Scottish Ministers are to appoint the first chief executive of the Commission on such terms and conditions as the Scottish Ministers may determine.3Before making the appointment of the first chief executive, the Scottish functions of that post.Staff81All staff employed, immediately before the coming into force of this sub-paragraph, by the Water Industry Commissioner for Scotland are transferred to the employment of schemes, andbmust, in any case, be approved by the Scottish Ministers.8The reference in sub-paragraph (6) to the provision of pensions, allowances or gratuities includes a reference to their provision by way of compensation for loss of office or employment or loss or diminution of emoluments.Transfer of property and liabilities91All property (including rights) and liabilities, subsisting immediately before the coming into force of this paragraph, of the Water Industry Commissioner for Scotland are transferred to the Commission.2Sub-paragraph (1) has effect in relation to any property and liabilities to which it applies despite any provision (of whatever nature) which would otherwise prevent, penalise or prohibit the transfer of the property or liabilities.Committees101The Commission may establish committees for or in connection with the exercise of such of its functions as it may determine.2Any committee established under this paragraph must be chaired by a person who is an ordinary member of the Commission.3Employees of the Commission who are not members of the Commission may be appointed to be members of any committee established by it.Delegation of powers111Anything authorised or required under any enactment to be done by the Commission may be done by any of its committees which, or by any of its members or employees who, are authorised (whether generally or specifically) by it for the purpose.2Nothing in sub-paragraph (1) prevents the Commission from doing anything that a committee, member or employee has been authorised or required to do.Proceedings121The Commission may regulate its own procedure (including any quorum) and that of any of its committees.2The validity of any proceedings or actings of the Commission is not affected by—aany vacancy among its members, orbany defect in the appointment of a member.General powers131The Commission may do anything which appears necessary or expedient for the purpose of, or in connection with, the exercise of its functions including, in particular—aentering into contracts; andbacquiring and disposing of property.2But the Commission may not acquire or dispose of land without the consent of the Scottish Ministers.Accounts14The Commission must—aprepare for each financial year, in accordance with directions given by the Scottish Ministers, an account of the Commission's income and expenditure, andbsend the account, by such time as the Scottish Ministers may direct, to the Auditor General for Scotland for auditing..

                            persons whose premises are connected to the public water supply system or the public sewerage system (within the meaning of Part 2 of the Water Services etc. (Scotland) Act 2005 (asp 3)) or both

                    Commission's

Part 1Water Industry Commission and Customer PanelsWater Industry Commission for Scotland11For section 1 (Water Industry Commissioner for Scotland) of the 2002 Act there is substituted—Water Industry Commission for Scotland11There is established a body to be known as the Water Industry Commission for Scotland (referred to in this Act as “the Commission”).2The Commission has the general function of promoting the interests of persons (taken as a whole) whose premises—aare connected to the public water supply system or the public sewerage system (within the meaning of Part 2 of the Water Services etc. (Scotland) Act 2005 (asp 3)) or both, orbmight reasonably become connected to either or both of those systems,relating to the provision to them of water and sewerage services.3The Scottish Ministers may, after consulting the Commission, give the Commission directions of a general or specific character as to the financial management or administration of the Commission; and the Commission must comply with any such directions.4Schedule A1 makes further provision about the Commission..2In section 4 (power of the Commissioner to require information) of that Act, for subsection (2) there is substituted—2Subsection (1) does not authorise the Commission to require the disclosure of anything which a person would be entitled to refuse to disclose on grounds of confidentiality in proceedings in the Court of Session.3Where Scottish Water considers that it is entitled to withhold information from the Commission—abecause it is not reasonably sought, orbby virtue of subsection (2),it must intimate that fact to the Commission in writing..3In section 5 (annual reports by the Commissioner etc.) of that Act, at the end there is added—4The Scottish Ministers must lay before the Parliament a copy of each report submitted to them under subsection (1)(a)..4Schedule 1 inserts schedule A1 into that Act.

Part 9Statutory nuisancesEnforcement of statutory nuisances: fixed penalty notice1131The 1990 Act is further amended as follows.2In section 80 (summary proceedings for statutory nuisances), after subsection (4), insert—4AWhere a local authority have reason to believe that a person has committed an offence under subsection (4) above, the local authority may give that person a notice (a “fixed penalty notice”) in accordance with section 80ZA offering the person the opportunity of discharging any liability to conviction for that offence by payment of a fixed penalty..3After that section, insert—Fixed penalty notice: supplemental80ZA1This section applies to a fixed penalty notice given under section 80(4A).2A fixed penalty notice must give reasonable particulars of the circumstances alleged to constitute the offence.3A fixed penalty notice must also state—athe amount of the fixed penalty;bthe period within which it may be paid;cthe—iperson to whom; andiiaddress at which,payment may be made;dthe method or methods by which payment may be made;ethe consequences of not making a payment within the period for payment.4The amount of the fixed penalty under section 80(4A) is—ain the case of a nuisance relating to industrial, trade or business premises, £400;bin any other case, £150.5The period for payment of the fixed penalty is 14 days beginning with the day after the day on which the notice is given.6The local authority may extend the period for paying the fixed penalty in any particular case if they consider it appropriate to do so by sending notice to the person to whom the fixed penalty notice was given.7No proceedings for an offence under section 80(4) may be commenced before the end of the period for payment of the fixed penalty.8In proceedings for an offence under section 80(4), a certificate which—apurports to be signed by or on behalf of a person having responsibility for the financial affairs of the local authority; andbstates that payment of the amount specified in the fixed penalty notice was or was not received by the expiry of the period within which that fixed penalty may be paid,is sufficient evidence of the facts stated.9Where proceedings for an offence in respect of which a fixed penalty notice has been given are commenced, the notice is to be treated as withdrawn.10Any sum received by a local authority under section 80(4A) accrues to that authority.11The Scottish Ministers may, by regulations—aprovide that fixed penalty notices may not be given in such circumstances as may be prescribed;bprovide for the form of a fixed penalty notice;cprovide for the method or methods by which fixed penalties may be paid;dmodify subsection (4)(a) or (b) above so as to substitute a different amount (not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale) for the amount for the time being specified there;eprovide for the amount of the fixed penalty to be different in different cases or descriptions of case;fmodify subsection (5) above so as to substitute a different period for the period for the time being specified there;gprovide for the keeping of accounts, and the preparation and publication of statements of account relating to fixed penalties under section 80(4A).12Before making regulations under subsection (11) above, the Scottish Ministers must consult, in so far as it is reasonably practicable to do so, the persons mentioned in subsection (13) below.13Those persons are—asuch associations of local authorities; andbsuch other persons,as the Scottish Ministers consider appropriate..4In section 81 (supplementary provisions), for subsection (3), substitute—3Where an abatement notice has not been complied with, the local authority may, whether or not—aproceedings have been taken for an offence under section 80(4); orba fixed penalty notice has been given under section 80(4A) in respect of that offence (regardless of whether the fixed penalty notice is accepted),abate the nuisance and do whatever may be necessary in execution of the abatement notice..

xmls: Part 7Reservoirs<Emphasis>Enforcement powers and incident reporting</Emphasis>Flood plans89After section 12B of the 1975 Act, insert—Flood plans: Scotland12C1The Scottish Ministers may by regulations made by statutory instrument provide that a flood plan is to be prepared for each reservoir in Scotland which meets criteria specified in, or otherwise determined in accordance with, the regulations.2A “flood plan” is a plan setting out the action to be taken by the undertaker of the reservoir to which the plan relates in order to control or mitigate the effects of flooding likely to result from any escape of water from the reservoir.3The regulations may, in particular—aprovide that the enforcement authority or another person—imay specify the criteria, andiiis to determine whether a reservoir meets the criteria,bspecify what is to be included in a flood plan and may, in particular, provide that a plan must include a map,cspecify the form in which a flood plan is to be prepared,dprovide that it is for the undertaker of a reservoir or other person to prepare a flood plan in relation to the reservoir,erequire the person preparing a flood plan to have regard to guidance issued by the enforcement authority or the Scottish Ministers,frequire the flood plan to be produced or submitted to the enforcement authority by such time as—ithe regulations specify, oriithe authority or Scottish Ministers may direct,gmake provision about the approval of flood plans,hmake provision for the review and updating of flood plans,iprovide for a register of flood plans to be established and maintained,jmake provision for the publication, or distribution of copies, of—ia list of reservoirs in relation to which a flood plan must be prepared by virtue of the regulations,iiflood plans, andiiireports,kmake provision in connection with the testing of flood plans,lrequire the undertaker of a reservoir to take action set out in the flood plan relating to the reservoir in the event of an emergency,mprovide that the enforcement authority may, in circumstances specified in the regulations, do anything that another person is required to do under the regulations and may recover the costs of doing so from that person,nconfer powers of entry on the enforcement authority in connection with its functions under the regulations,omake provision in connection with paragraphs (m) and (n) amending this Act (other than this section) or applying this Act with modifications,pcreate offences,qprovide that any offence created is triable—ionly summarily, oriieither summarily or on indictment,rprovide for any offence created which is triable only summarily to be punishable on conviction by a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale,sprovide for any offence created which is triable either summarily or on indictment to be punishable—ion summary conviction, by a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum,iion conviction on indictment, by a fine.4Before making regulations under subsection (1), the Scottish Ministers must consult—aSEPA,bundertakers of reservoirs for which they consider a flood plan will require to be prepared under the regulations,cthe Institution of Civil Engineers, anddsuch other persons as they consider appropriate.5The power to make regulations under subsection (1) may be exercised so as to make different provision for different purposes.6A statutory instrument made under subsection (1) is not to be made unless a draft of the instrument has been laid before, and approved by resolution of, the Scottish Parliament..

xmls: PART 2Fire reform<Emphasis>The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service</Emphasis>The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service1011After section 1 of the 2005 Act, insert—The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service1A1There is established a body corporate to be known as the Scottish Fire and Rescue Serviceor, in Gaelic, Seirbheis Smàlaidh agus Teasairginn na h-Alba (referred to in this Act as “SFRS”).2SFRS has the functions conferred on it by or under this Act or any other enactment.3Schedule 1A makes further provision about SFRS..2After schedule 1 to the 2005 Act, insert—SCHEDULE 1AThe Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (introduced by section 1A(3))<Emphasis>Status</Emphasis>11SFRS—ais not a servant or agent of the Crown, andbhas no status, immunity or privilege of the Crown.2SFRS's property is not property of, or property held on behalf of, the Crown.<Emphasis>Membership</Emphasis>21SFRS is to consist of—aa member appointed by the Scottish Ministers to chair SFRS (“the chairing member”), andbnot fewer than 10 nor more than 14 other members appointed by the Scottish Ministers.2The Scottish Ministers may appoint as members only persons who they consider to have skills and expertise relevant to the functions of SFRS.3The Scottish Ministers may by order modify sub-paragraph (1)(b) by substituting for the minimum or maximum number of members for the time being specified such other number as they think fit.4Members of SFRS may elect from their number a member to act as deputy to the chairing member.<Emphasis>Disqualification</Emphasis>31A person is disqualified from appointment, and from holding office, as a member of SFRS if that person is or becomes—aa member of staff of SFRS,ba member ofithe Scottish Parliament,iithe House of Lords,iiithe House of Commons, orivthe European Parliament,cdisqualified from standing for election as a member ofithe Scottish Parliament,iithe House of Commons, oriiia local authority.2The Scottish Ministers may by order modify sub-paragraph (1).<Emphasis>Tenure</Emphasis>41A member is to be appointed for a period not exceeding 4 years specified in the appointment.2A member holds and vacates office on such terms and conditions as the Scottish Ministers may determine.3On ceasing to be a member, a person is eligible for reappointment.4A member may, by notice in writing to the Scottish Ministers, resign office as a member.<Emphasis>Removal from office</Emphasis>51The Scottish Ministers may remove a member from office if—athe member is an undischarged bankrupt,bthe member has, without reasonable excuse, been absent from meetings of SFRS for a period longer than 4 consecutive months,cthe member has, without reasonable excuse, been absent from 3 consecutive meetings of SFRS,dthe member has been convicted (whether before or after the member's appointment) of a criminal offence,ethe member has failed to comply with the terms or conditions of the member's appointment,fthe Scottish Ministers consider that the member is otherwise unfit to be a member or is unable for any reason to carry out the member's functions.2For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1)(a), “undischarged bankrupt” means a person—awhose estate has been sequestrated and who has not been discharged (or against whom a bankruptcy order has been made and is still in force),bwho has granted a trust deed for, or made a composition or arrangement with, creditors (and has not been discharged in respect of it),cwho is the subject of a bankruptcy restrictions order, or an interim bankruptcy restrictions order, made under the Bankruptcy (Scotland) Act 1985 (c.66) or the Insolvency Act 1986 (c.45),dwho is the subject of a bankruptcy restrictions undertaking entered into under either of those Acts,ewho has been adjudged bankrupt (and has not been discharged), orfwho is subject to any other kind of order, arrangement or undertaking analogous to those mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (d), anywhere in the world.<Emphasis>Remuneration, allowances and expenses of members</Emphasis>6SFRS may pay to its members such remuneration, allowances and expenses as the Scottish Ministers may determine.<Emphasis>The Chief Officer</Emphasis>71SFRS must employ a Chief Officer.2The Chief Officer may not be a member of SFRS.3The first Chief Officer is to be appointed by the Scottish Ministers on such terms and conditions as they may determine.4Each subsequent appointment of a person as the Chief Officer is to be made by SFRS.5The appointment of a person under sub-paragraph (4) is subject to the approval of the Scottish Ministers.6The terms and conditions of a person appointed under sub-paragraph (4) are to be determined by SFRS.<Emphasis>SFRS's employees</Emphasis>81SFRS may employ staff.2Staff are to be employed on terms and conditions determined by SFRS.3SFRS may pay or make arrangements for the payment of pensions, allowances or gratuities to, or in respect of, any person who is, or has ceased to be, a member of staff (including the Chief Officer).4The reference in sub-paragraph (3) to pensions, allowances and gratuities includes pensions, allowances and gratuities by way of compensation for loss of employment.5The arrangements mentioned in sub-paragraph (3) may include—athe making of contributions or payments towards provision for pensions, allowances or gratuities mentioned there, andbthe establishment and administration of pension schemes.<Emphasis>Committees and sub-committees</Emphasis>91SFRS may establish committees for any purpose.2Any committee so established may establish sub-committees.3The members of any committee or sub-committee may include persons who are not members of SFRS but such persons are not entitled to vote at meetings.4A committee or sub-committee must not consist entirely of persons who are not members of SFRS.5SFRS may pay such remuneration, allowances and expenses as are determined by SFRS to a member of a committee or sub-committee who is not—aa member of SFRS, orba member of staff of SFRS.<Emphasis>Procedure</Emphasis>101SFRS may regulate—aits own procedure (including quorum), andbthe procedure (including quorum) of its committees and sub-committees.2The validity of any proceedings or acts of SFRS is not affected by any—avacancy in its membership,bdefect in the appointment of a member,cdisqualification of a person as a member after appointment.<Emphasis>Public access</Emphasis>111SFRS must ensure that its proceedings and those of its committees and sub-committees are held in public.2Despite sub-paragraph (1), SFRS or, as the case may be, any of its committees or sub-committees may decide to hold all or part of any proceedings in private.3SFRS must publish—aagendas for its proceedings and those of its committees and sub-committees,bthe papers relating to those proceedings,csuch reports of those proceedings as it thinks fit.4Despite sub-paragraph (3), SFRS may decide that all or part of any agenda, paper or report need not be published.5SFRS must publish a statement setting out—athe circumstances in which its proceedings and those of its committees and sub-committees may be held in private, andbthe circumstances in which agendas, papers and reports need not be published.<Emphasis>Governance and accountability</Emphasis>12SFRS must try to ensure that each of its members, when acting in the capacity of member—aacts consistently with any principle of good governance which appears to SFRS to constitute best practice, andbacts in a way which is as accountable and transparent as is reasonably practicable.<Emphasis>SFRS's general powers</Emphasis>131SFRS may do anything that it considers appropriate for the purposes of, or in connection with, the carrying out of its functions.2SFRS may in particular—aenter into contracts,bborrow money,cacquire and dispose of land and other property,dwith the authorisation of the Scottish Ministers, purchase compulsorily land,eform or promote (whether alone or with another) companies under the Companies Act 2006 (c.46).3SFRS may not exercise the power in sub-paragraph (2)(b) or (e) without the consent of the Scottish Ministers.4For the purposes of sub-paragraph (3) consent may be given—awith respect to a particular case or class of case,bsubject to such conditions as the Scottish Ministers consider appropriate.5The power in sub-paragraph (2)(c) includes the power to accept, on such conditions as SFRS considers appropriate—agifts of money, andbgifts or loans of other property.6The powers in sub-paragraph (2)(c) and (d) to acquire and purchase land include power to acquire a servitude or other right in or over land by the creation of a new right.7The Acquisition of Land (Authorisation Procedure) (Scotland) Act 1947 (c.42) applies in relation to the compulsory purchase of land under sub-paragraph (2)(d) as if—athat sub-paragraph were contained in an Act in force immediately before the commencement of that Act, andbSFRS were a local authority.<Emphasis>Delegation of functions</Emphasis>141SFRS may delegate any of its functions to a person mentioned in sub-paragraph (2).2Those persons are—athe Chief Officer,bany other member of staff of SFRS,cany of its committees.3Sub-paragraph (1) does not affect—aSFRS's responsibility for the carrying out of the delegated functions, orbSFRS's ability to carry out the delegated functions.<Emphasis>Location of principal office premises</Emphasis>15Any determination by SFRS as to the location of the principal office premises of its members or its Chief Officer is subject to the approval of the Scottish Ministers.<Emphasis>Grants</Emphasis>161The Scottish Ministers may make grants to SFRS of such amounts as they may determine.2A grant is made subject to any conditions specified by the Scottish Ministers (including conditions about repayment).<Emphasis>Accounts</Emphasis>171SFRS must—akeep proper accounts and accounting records, andbprepare for each financial year a statement of accounts.2Each statement of accounts must comply with any directions given by the Scottish Ministers as to—athe information to be contained in it,bthe manner in which the information is to be presented,cthe methods and principles according to which the statement is to be prepared.3SFRS must send each statement of accounts to the Auditor General for Scotland for auditing.4In this paragraph, “financial year” means—athe period beginning on the day on which SFRS is established and ending on 31 March next occurring, andbeach subsequent period of a year ending on 31 March..

DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asp/2024/15/section/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asp/2024/15/section/1" id="section-1"><Pnumber><CommentaryRef Ref="key-74144e"/>1</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asp/2024/15/section/1/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asp/2024/15/section/1/1" id="section-1-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The <Citation URI="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/asp/2009/12" id="c00001" Class="ScottishAct" Year="2009" Number="12">Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009</Citation> is modified as follows.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/asp/2024/15/section/1/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/asp/2024/15/section/1/2" id="section-1-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After <ExternalLink URI="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/asp/2009/12/section/A1">section A1</ExternalLink> insert—</Text><BlockAmendment Context="main" Format="double" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown"><Pblock><Title>Scottish carbon budgets</Title><P1group><Title>Scottish carbon budgets and associated concepts</Title><P1 id="p00178"><Pnumber>A2</Pnumber><P1para><P2 id="p00180"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A Scottish carbon budget is the number of tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent prescribed for a given period.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The Scottish carbon budget for a period is exceeded if the net Scottish emissions account for the period exceeds the number of tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent prescribed for the period.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 id="p00188"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Not exceeding a Scottish carbon budget is referred to in this Act as a “Scottish carbon budget target”.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 id="p00192"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where this Act refers to an emissions reduction target for a year, the reference is to be construed in the context of a Scottish carbon budget target as follows—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the year in question is the final year of the period covered by the Scottish carbon budget giving rise to the target, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the target for the year is met if that budget has not been exceeded.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 id="p00204"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this section, “<Term>prescribed</Term>” means prescribed by virtue of regulations under <InternalLink Ref="p00215">section A4</InternalLink>.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Duty of Scottish Ministers in relation to budgets</Title><P1 id="p00210"><Pnumber>A3</Pnumber><P1para><Text>The Scottish Ministers must ensure that each Scottish carbon budget target is met.</Text></P1para></P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Budget-setting regulations</Title><P1 id="p00215"><Pnumber>A4</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The Scottish Ministers must, by regulations, set Scottish carbon budgets so that every year between 2026 and the net-zero emissions target year is covered by a budget.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A budget for a period—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may be set by expressing the prescribed number of tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent for the period either as a figure or as a method for calculating a figure, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may, in particular, be set by expressing the number as a proportion of the baseline multiplied by the number of years comprising the period.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 id="p00233"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The period covered by a Scottish carbon budget—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>is to be 5 years (for example 2026 to 2030), but</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may be shorter in the case of the budget for the period that ends with the net-zero emissions target year.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 id="p00245"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In preparing a draft of regulations to be made under this section, the Scottish Ministers must—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>have regard to the target-setting criteria, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>take into account the most up-to-date advice they have received from the relevant body.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 id="p00257"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>On the same day as laying before the Scottish Parliament for approval a draft of regulations under this section, the Scottish Ministers must publish a statement setting out in respect of each Scottish carbon budget that would be set by the regulations—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the extent to which the proposed budget takes account of the target-setting criteria, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>whether the proposed budget is in accordance with the most up-to-date advice the Ministers have received from the relevant body and, if it is not, the reasons why.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A statement under <InternalLink Ref="p00257">subsection (5)</InternalLink> must also set out, in indicative terms, the proposals and policies in relation to each of the sectors mentioned in section 35(3) which are likely (if the regulations are approved) to be set out in the next climate change plan due to be laid before the Scottish Parliament under section 35(1).</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A statement under <InternalLink Ref="p00257">subsection (5)</InternalLink> must also state whether the Scottish Ministers expect that, during the period covered by a Scottish carbon budget that would be set by the regulations, the net Scottish emissions account for a year will, for the first time since this section came into force, be—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>75% lower than the baseline,</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>90% lower than the baseline.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Alteration of budget periods</Title><P1><Pnumber>A5</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The Scottish Ministers may by regulations modify <InternalLink Ref="p00215">section A4</InternalLink><InternalLink Ref="p00233">(3)</InternalLink> so as to alter the length of the periods to be covered by Scottish carbon budgets.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The power under this section may be exercised only if it appears to the Scottish Ministers necessary to do so in order to keep the periods covered by Scottish carbon budgets in line with similar periods under any international agreement to which the United Kingdom is a party.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Before laying before the Scottish Parliament for approval a draft of regulations under this section, the Scottish Ministers must consult the relevant body.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 A4</InternalLink>;</Text></P3para></P3></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Chapter></Part></Body></Primary></Legislation>

Format="default"><P1group><Title><Emphasis>Destination of proceeds – Wales</Emphasis></Title><P1><Pnumber PuncAfter="">4A</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>This paragraph applies to regulations made by the Welsh Ministers in relation to Wales.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The regulations may provide for the application of the net proceeds of the charge to specified purposes.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under sub-paragraph (2) may (among other things)–</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>require sellers to apply the net proceeds of the charge to any one or more specified purposes;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>provide for any duty imposed under paragraph (a) to be discharged (subject to any provision made under paragraph (c)) by the net proceeds of the charge being accepted by any one or more of the following persons–</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>specified persons;</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>persons who fall within a specified category of person;</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>make provision about the arrangements under which the net proceeds of the charge are to be given by sellers to the persons mentioned in paragraph (b) or any other person;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>require persons who accept any net proceeds of the charge under paragraph (b) to apply the proceeds to any one or more specified purposes;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>e</Pnumber><P3para><Text>provide for recovery by the Welsh Ministers of sums equal to the proceeds of the charge that have been accepted or applied otherwise than in accordance with provision made under sub-paragraph (2);</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>f</Pnumber><P3para><Text>provide for the application of sums recovered under paragraph (e) to specified purposes (this includes making provision to the effect that such sums are not to be paid into the Welsh Consolidated Fund);</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>g</Pnumber><P3para><Text>require the Welsh Ministers to give guidance about compliance with the regulations.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The purposes that may be specified under sub-paragraph (2) are limited to purposes relating to any of the following–</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>preventing or reducing waste;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the collection, management, treatment or disposal of waste;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>protecting or improving the environment in relation to pollution or nuisances;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>educational or recreational activities for children or young people which relate to any of the matters specified in paragraphs (a) to (c).</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>But purposes concerning the production of renewable energy for consumption in transport or the use of that energy in transport may not be specified under sub-paragraph (2).</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The regulations may make provision for regulations under this Schedule to apply to persons other than sellers, if the Welsh Ministers consider that such provision is appropriate for the enforcement of provision made under sub-paragraph (2) or for otherwise making such provision effective.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The specified factors under paragraph 3(2)(c) may also include–</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>a seller's arrangements for applying the net proceeds of the charge, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>any other factor that the Welsh Ministers consider appropriate, whether or not that factor is of the same kind as the factors listed in that paragraph.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The regulations may provide for exceptions and exemptions.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group><P1group><Title><Emphasis>Interpretation of paragraph 4A</Emphasis></Title><P1><Pnumber PuncAfter="">4B</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>This paragraph applies for the purposes of paragraph 4A.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>“<Term>Children</Term>” means persons who have not attained the age of 18.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>“<Term>Pollution</Term>” means pollution of the air, water or land which may give rise to any environmental harm, including (but not limited to) pollution caused by light, noise, heat or vibrations or any other kind of release of energy.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For the purposes of the definition in sub-paragraph (3),  “<Term>environmental harm</Term>” means any of the following–</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>harm to the health of humans and other living organisms;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>harm to the quality of the environment, including–</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>harm to the quality of the environment taken as a whole,</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>harm to the quality of the air, water or land, and</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>iii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>other impairment of, or interference with, the ecological systems of which any living organisms form part;</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>offence to the senses of human beings;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>damage to property;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>e</Pnumber><P3para><Text>impairment of, or interference with, the amenity of the environment or any legitimate use of the environment.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For the purposes of sub-paragraphs (3) and (4),  “<Term>air</Term>” includes (but is not limited to) air within buildings and air within other natural or man-made structures above or below ground.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>“<Term>Nuisance</Term>” means an act or omission affecting any place, or a state of affairs in any place, which may impair, or interfere with, the amenity of the environment or any legitimate use of the environment.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>“<Term>Net proceeds of the charge</Term>” has the same meaning as in paragraph 7(4).</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>“<Term>Young people</Term>” means persons who have attained the age of 18, but not the age of 25.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/mwa/2010/8/section/1/3" 4A(2).</Text></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/mwa/2010/8/section/1/4" person.</Text></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>
