law.title: Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels Regulations (Northern Ireland)

the 2013 regulations.title: Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2013

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147" NumberOfProvisions="13" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/body" NumberOfProvisions="13" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Amendment of the Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2007</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/2" id="regulation-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>The Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2007<FootnoteRef Ref="f00004"/> are amended in accordance with regulations 3 to 8.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of regulation 2 (interpretation)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/3" id="regulation-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 2 (interpretation) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>

<P2para><Text>In these Regulations—</Text><UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“combustion plant” means any technical apparatus in which fuels are oxidised in order to use the heat generated;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“Council Directive 1999/32/EC” means Council Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1999/0032" id="c00001" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="1999" Number="32">1999/32/EC</Citation> relating to a reduction in the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels and amending Council Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1993/0012" id="c00002" Class="EuropeanEconomicCommunityDirective" Year="1993" Number="12">93/12/EEC</Citation>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“gas oil” means any petroleum-derived liquid fuel—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>that falls within CN code 2710 19 25, 2710 19 29, 2710 19 47, 2710 19 48, 2710 20 17 or 2710 20 19; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>of which less than 65 per cent by volume (including losses) distils at 250°C and of which at least 85 per cent by volume (including losses) distils at 350°C by the ASTM D86 method,</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
<Text>but excluding marine fuels, diesel fuels (as defined by Article 2(2) of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1998/0070" id="c00003" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="1998" Number="70">98/70/EC</Citation> of the European Parliament and of the Council relating to the quality of petrol and diesel fuels and amending Council Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1993/0012" id="c00004" Class="EuropeanEconomicCommunityDirective" Year="1993" Number="12">93/12/EEC</Citation>) and fuels used in non-road mobile machinery and agricultural tractors;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“heavy fuel oil” means any petroleum-derived liquid fuel—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>that falls within CN code 2710 19 51 to 2710 19 68, 2710 20 31, 2710 20 35 or 2710 20 39;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>which, by reason of its distillation limits, falls within the category of heavy oils intended for use as fuel and of which less than 65 per cent by volume (including losses) distils at 250°C by the ASTM D86 method; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>where the distillation cannot be determined by the ASTM D86 method, that is categorised as heavy fuel oil,</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
<Text>but excluding marine fuel and gas oil;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“marine fuel” means any petroleum-derived liquid fuel intended for use or in use on board a vessel, including those fuels defined in ISO 8217;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“sulphur content of liquid fuels permit” has the meaning given in regulation 4(5)(b);</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“the 2013 Regulations” means the Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2013;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>In paragraph (1)—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>“ASTM method” means a method laid down by the American Society for Testing and Materials in the 1976 edition of standard definitions and specifications for petroleum and lubricating products; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>the reference to a numbered CN code is a reference to the code set out in Annex I to Council Regulation 2658/87 on the tariff and statistical nomenclature and on the Common Customs Tariff;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Expressions used in these Regulations that also appear in Council Directive 1999/32/EC relating to a reduction in the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels as amended by Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2005/0033" id="c00005" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2005" Number="33">2005/33/EC</Citation> of the European Parliament and of the Council have the same meaning as they do in that Directive.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Interpretation Act (Northern Ireland) 1954 applies to these regulations as it applies to an Act of the Assembly.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of Regulation 4 (maximum sulphur content of heavy fuel oil)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/4" id="regulation-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 4 (maximum sulphur content of heavy fuel oil) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">4</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>

<P2para><Text>No person shall use any heavy fuel oil that has a sulphur content exceeding 1 per cent by mass.</Text></P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Until 1st January 2016, paragraph (1) shall not apply to the use of heavy fuel oil—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a new plant that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is subject to Article 4(1) of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00006" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation> and is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out for new plants in Part A of Annex IV of that Directive; or</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is subject to Article 4(2) of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00007" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation> and is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out for new plants in Part B of Annex IV of that Directive;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in an existing plant—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out for new plants in Part A of Annex IV of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00008" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation>; or</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>that is a participating plant operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average emissions of sulphur dioxide from the plant from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average of emissions of sulphur dioxide from the plant from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis; or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a gas engine, a gas turbine or a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>forms part of a refinery; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that the monthly average of emissions of sulphur dioxide averaged over all combustion plants in the refinery, irrespective of the type of fuel or fuel combination used, does not exceed 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3 </Superior>at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis.</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>From 1st January 2016, paragraph (1) shall not apply to the use of heavy fuel oil—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>falls within the scope of Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out in Annex V to that Directive;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>falls within the scope of Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is not subject to the emission limit values for sulphur dioxide set out in Annex V to that Directive; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>iii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average emissions of sulphur dioxide from the plant from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average emissions of sulphur dioxide from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis; or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a gas engine, a gas turbine or a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>forms part of a refinery; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that the monthly average of emissions of sulphur dioxide averaged over all combustion plants in the refinery, irrespective of the type of fuel or fuel combination used, does not exceed 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis.</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The enforcing authority that grants a permit referred to in paragraph (2) or (3) shall carry out appropriate monitoring of emissions of sulphur dioxide to ensure that the limitations on emissions contained in that permit are not exceeded.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>In this regulation—</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00009" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation>” means Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00010" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation> of the European Parliament and of the Council on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the air from large combustion plants;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“Directive 2010/75/EU” means Directive 2010/75/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on industrial emissions (integrated pollution prevention and control) (Recast);</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“existing plant” and “new plant” have the meanings given in Article 2(10) and 2(9) respectively of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00011" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“gas engine” and “gas turbine” have the meaning given in Article 3(34) and 3(33) respectively of Directive 2010/75/EU;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“participating plant” has the meaning given in regulation 3(1)(c) of the Large Combustion Plants (National Emission Reduction Plan) Regulations 2007;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“permit” means—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>if the operation of the combustion plant requires an authorisation or permit—</Text><OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="roman">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>an authorisation under Article 6 of the Industrial Pollution and Control (Northern Ireland) Order 1997; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a permit granted under regulation 10 of the 2013 Regulations;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
<Text>or</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a sulphur content of liquid fuels permit which—</Text><OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="roman">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>was granted for the purposes of the Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels (Northern Ireland) Regulations 2002 and which is still subsisting; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>is granted under these Regulations.</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Schedule 1 (Sulphur content of liquid fuels permits) has effect.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of Regulation 5 (maximum sulphur content in gas oil)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/5" id="regulation-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 5 (maximum sulphur content in gas oil) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">5</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>No person shall use any gas oil that has a sulphur content exceeding 0.1 per cent by mass.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of Regulation 6 (sampling and analysis)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/6/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/6" id="regulation-6">
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 6 (sampling and analysis) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">6</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>

<P2para><Text>The Department shall take all necessary measures to ensure that periodic sampling is carried out of heavy fuel oil and gas oil and that the samples are analysed to check that the use of those fuels complies with regulations 4(1) and 5.</Text></P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Sampling shall be carried out with sufficient frequency and in such a way that the Department is satisfied that the samples are representative of the fuels examined.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The samples shall be analysed without undue delay.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The reference method adopted for determining the sulphur content of fuels sampled pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be defined by ISO method 8754 (2003) or EN ISO 14596 (2007).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment to Schedule 1 (sulphur content of liquid fuel permits)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7" id="regulation-7">
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/1" id="regulation-7-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Schedule 1 (sulphur content of liquid fuel permits) is amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/2" id="regulation-7-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In the heading to that Schedule for “Regulation 4(5)” substitute “Regulation 4(6)”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/3" id="regulation-7-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraph 1 for the words “an existing plant, new plant or other combustion plant” substitute “a combustion plant”, and after “regulation 4(2)” add “or 4(3)”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/4" id="regulation-7-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraph 2(c) after “regulation 4(2)” add “or 4(3)”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/5" id="regulation-7-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>For paragraph 9 substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">9</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>Regulation 7 of the 2013 Regulations (Discharge and scope of functions) shall apply to functions under these Regulations as it applies to functions under the 2013 Regulations.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

law.title: Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels Regulations (Northern Ireland)

the 2013 regulations.title: Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2013

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147" NumberOfProvisions="13" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/body" NumberOfProvisions="13" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Amendment of the Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2007</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/2" id="regulation-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>The Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2007<FootnoteRef Ref="f00004"/> are amended in accordance with regulations 3 to 8.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of regulation 2 (interpretation)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/3" id="regulation-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 2 (interpretation) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>

<P2para><Text>In these Regulations—</Text><UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“combustion plant” means any technical apparatus in which fuels are oxidised in order to use the heat generated;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“Council Directive 1999/32/EC” means Council Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1999/0032" id="c00001" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="1999" Number="32">1999/32/EC</Citation> relating to a reduction in the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels and amending Council Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1993/0012" id="c00002" Class="EuropeanEconomicCommunityDirective" Year="1993" Number="12">93/12/EEC</Citation>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“gas oil” means any petroleum-derived liquid fuel—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>that falls within CN code 2710 19 25, 2710 19 29, 2710 19 47, 2710 19 48, 2710 20 17 or 2710 20 19; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>of which less than 65 per cent by volume (including losses) distils at 250°C and of which at least 85 per cent by volume (including losses) distils at 350°C by the ASTM D86 method,</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
<Text>but excluding marine fuels, diesel fuels (as defined by Article 2(2) of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1998/0070" id="c00003" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="1998" Number="70">98/70/EC</Citation> of the European Parliament and of the Council relating to the quality of petrol and diesel fuels and amending Council Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1993/0012" id="c00004" Class="EuropeanEconomicCommunityDirective" Year="1993" Number="12">93/12/EEC</Citation>) and fuels used in non-road mobile machinery and agricultural tractors;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“heavy fuel oil” means any petroleum-derived liquid fuel—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>that falls within CN code 2710 19 51 to 2710 19 68, 2710 20 31, 2710 20 35 or 2710 20 39;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>which, by reason of its distillation limits, falls within the category of heavy oils intended for use as fuel and of which less than 65 per cent by volume (including losses) distils at 250°C by the ASTM D86 method; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>where the distillation cannot be determined by the ASTM D86 method, that is categorised as heavy fuel oil,</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
<Text>but excluding marine fuel and gas oil;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“marine fuel” means any petroleum-derived liquid fuel intended for use or in use on board a vessel, including those fuels defined in ISO 8217;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“sulphur content of liquid fuels permit” has the meaning given in regulation 4(5)(b);</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“the 2013 Regulations” means the Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2013;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>In paragraph (1)—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>“ASTM method” means a method laid down by the American Society for Testing and Materials in the 1976 edition of standard definitions and specifications for petroleum and lubricating products; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>the reference to a numbered CN code is a reference to the code set out in Annex I to Council Regulation 2658/87 on the tariff and statistical nomenclature and on the Common Customs Tariff;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Expressions used in these Regulations that also appear in Council Directive 1999/32/EC relating to a reduction in the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels as amended by Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2005/0033" id="c00005" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2005" Number="33">2005/33/EC</Citation> of the European Parliament and of the Council have the same meaning as they do in that Directive.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Interpretation Act (Northern Ireland) 1954 applies to these regulations as it applies to an Act of the Assembly.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of Regulation 4 (maximum sulphur content of heavy fuel oil)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/4" id="regulation-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 4 (maximum sulphur content of heavy fuel oil) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">4</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>

<P2para><Text>No person shall use any heavy fuel oil that has a sulphur content exceeding 1 per cent by mass.</Text></P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Until 1st January 2016, paragraph (1) shall not apply to the use of heavy fuel oil—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a new plant that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is subject to Article 4(1) of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00006" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation> and is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out for new plants in Part A of Annex IV of that Directive; or</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is subject to Article 4(2) of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00007" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation> and is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out for new plants in Part B of Annex IV of that Directive;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in an existing plant—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out for new plants in Part A of Annex IV of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00008" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation>; or</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>that is a participating plant operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average emissions of sulphur dioxide from the plant from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average of emissions of sulphur dioxide from the plant from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis; or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a gas engine, a gas turbine or a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>forms part of a refinery; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that the monthly average of emissions of sulphur dioxide averaged over all combustion plants in the refinery, irrespective of the type of fuel or fuel combination used, does not exceed 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3 </Superior>at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis.</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>From 1st January 2016, paragraph (1) shall not apply to the use of heavy fuel oil—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>falls within the scope of Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that emission limit values for sulphur dioxide are at least as stringent as those set out in Annex V to that Directive;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>falls within the scope of Chapter III of Directive 2010/75/EU;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is not subject to the emission limit values for sulphur dioxide set out in Annex V to that Directive; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>iii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average emissions of sulphur dioxide from the plant from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis;</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition prohibiting the monthly average emissions of sulphur dioxide from exceeding 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis; or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a combustion plant, other than a gas engine, a gas turbine or a plant to which sub-paragraph (a) or (b) applies, that—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>forms part of a refinery; and</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>is operated in accordance with a permit containing a condition that the monthly average of emissions of sulphur dioxide averaged over all combustion plants in the refinery, irrespective of the type of fuel or fuel combination used, does not exceed 1,700 mg/Nm<Superior>3</Superior> at an oxygen content in the flue gas of 3 per cent by volume on a dry basis.</Text></P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The enforcing authority that grants a permit referred to in paragraph (2) or (3) shall carry out appropriate monitoring of emissions of sulphur dioxide to ensure that the limitations on emissions contained in that permit are not exceeded.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>In this regulation—</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00009" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation>” means Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00010" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation> of the European Parliament and of the Council on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the air from large combustion plants;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“Directive 2010/75/EU” means Directive 2010/75/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on industrial emissions (integrated pollution prevention and control) (Recast);</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“existing plant” and “new plant” have the meanings given in Article 2(10) and 2(9) respectively of Directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2001/0080" id="c00011" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2001" Number="80">2001/80/EC</Citation>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“gas engine” and “gas turbine” have the meaning given in Article 3(34) and 3(33) respectively of Directive 2010/75/EU;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“participating plant” has the meaning given in regulation 3(1)(c) of the Large Combustion Plants (National Emission Reduction Plan) Regulations 2007;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“permit” means—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>if the operation of the combustion plant requires an authorisation or permit—</Text><OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="roman">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>an authorisation under Article 6 of the Industrial Pollution and Control (Northern Ireland) Order 1997; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a permit granted under regulation 10 of the 2013 Regulations;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
<Text>or</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a sulphur content of liquid fuels permit which—</Text><OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="roman">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>was granted for the purposes of the Sulphur Content of Liquid Fuels (Northern Ireland) Regulations 2002 and which is still subsisting; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>is granted under these Regulations.</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Schedule 1 (Sulphur content of liquid fuels permits) has effect.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of Regulation 5 (maximum sulphur content in gas oil)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/5" id="regulation-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 5 (maximum sulphur content in gas oil) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">5</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>No person shall use any gas oil that has a sulphur content exceeding 0.1 per cent by mass.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment of Regulation 6 (sampling and analysis)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/6/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/6" id="regulation-6">
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>For regulation 6 (sampling and analysis) substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">6</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>

<P2para><Text>The Department shall take all necessary measures to ensure that periodic sampling is carried out of heavy fuel oil and gas oil and that the samples are analysed to check that the use of those fuels complies with regulations 4(1) and 5.</Text></P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Sampling shall be carried out with sufficient frequency and in such a way that the Department is satisfied that the samples are representative of the fuels examined.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The samples shall be analysed without undue delay.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The reference method adopted for determining the sulphur content of fuels sampled pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be defined by ISO method 8754 (2003) or EN ISO 14596 (2007).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group><Title>Amendment to Schedule 1 (sulphur content of liquid fuel permits)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7" id="regulation-7">
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/1" id="regulation-7-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Schedule 1 (sulphur content of liquid fuel permits) is amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/2" id="regulation-7-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In the heading to that Schedule for “Regulation 4(5)” substitute “Regulation 4(6)”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/3" id="regulation-7-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraph 1 for the words “an existing plant, new plant or other combustion plant” substitute “a combustion plant”, and after “regulation 4(2)” add “or 4(3)”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/4" id="regulation-7-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In paragraph 2(c) after “regulation 4(2)” add “or 4(3)”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/147/regulation/7/5" id="regulation-7-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>For paragraph 9 substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">9</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>Regulation 7 of the 2013 Regulations (Discharge and scope of functions) shall apply to functions under these Regulations as it applies to functions under the 2013 Regulations.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

law.title: Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland)

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/304" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/304" NumberOfProvisions="39" RestrictStartDate="2014-12-10" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="N.I."><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/304/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/304/body" NumberOfProvisions="19" RestrictStartDate="2014-12-10" NumberFormat="default" RestrictExtent="N.I."><P1group RestrictStartDate="2014-12-10" RestrictExtent="N.I."><Title>Amendment of the Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2013</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/304/regulation/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/304/regulation/2" id="regulation-2">
<Pnumber><CommentaryRef Ref="key-a4ac8c"/>2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>The Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2013<FootnoteRef Ref="f00002"/> are amended in accordance with regulations 3 to 13.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group RestrictStartDate="2014-12-10" RestrictExtent="N.I."><Title>Amendment of regulation 2 (interpretation: general)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/304/regulation/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/304/regulation/3" id="regulation-3">
<Pnumber><CommentaryRef Ref="key-54b79f"/>3</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In regulation 2, at the appropriate alphabetical places, insert the following definitions—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“cogeneration” means the simultaneous generation in one process of thermal energy and electrical or mechanical energy;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“cost-benefit analysis” means a cost-benefit analysis carried out in accordance with Part 2 of Annex <Acronym Expansion="9">IX</Acronym> of the Energy Efficiency Directive;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“Energy Efficiency Directive” means Directive 2012/27/<Acronym Expansion="European Union">EU</Acronym> of the European Parliament and of the Council on energy efficiency amending Directives <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2009/0125" id="c00001" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2009" Number="125">2009/125/<Acronym Expansion="European Community">EC</Acronym></Citation> and 2010/30/EU and repealing Directives <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2004/0008" id="c00002" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2004" Number="8">2004/8/EC</Citation> and <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/2006/0032" id="c00003" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="2006" Number="32">2006/32/EC</Citation><Strong/><FootnoteRef Ref="f00003"/><Strong/>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“high-efficiency cogeneration” means cogeneration meeting the criteria laid down in Annex <Acronym Expansion="2">II</Acronym> of the Energy Efficiency Directive;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“net rated thermal input” means the rate at which fuel can be burned at the maximum continuous rating of the appliance multiplied by the net calorific value of the fuel and expressed as megawatts;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“rated thermal input” means the rate at which fuel can be burned at the maximum continuous rating of the appliance multiplied by the gross calorific value of the fuel and expressed as megawatts;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group><P1group RestrictStartDate="2014-12-10" RestrictExtent="N.I."><Title>Amendment of regulation 7 (discharge and scope of functions)</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2014/304/regulation/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2014/304/regulation/4" id="regulation-4">

law.title: Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland)

xmls:
SCHEDULE Schedule to be inserted as Schedule 13A to the Pollution Prevention and Control (Industrial Emissions) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2013 Regulation 13 SCHEDULE 13A ENERGY EFFICIENCY DIRECTIVE Regulation 7 Application 1 This Schedule applies to every installation or mobile plant to which Article 14(5) of the Energy Efficiency Directive applies. Interpretation 2 In this Schedule— “economically justified demand” means demand that does not exceed the needs for heating or cooling and which would otherwise be satisfied at market conditions by energy generation processes other than cogeneration; “electricity from cogeneration” means electricity generated in a process linked to the production of useful heat and calculated in accordance with the methodology laid down in Annex II of the Energy Efficiency Directive; “substantial refurbishment” means a refurbishment whose cost exceeds 50% of the investment cost for a new comparable unit, but the fitting of equipment to carry out the activity falling within head (a) of Part A of section 6.10 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 shall not be considered as refurbishment for the purposes of paragraphs 4, 7 and 10 of this Schedule; and “unit” means any boilers, furnaces, kilns, turbines or engines forming part of an installation which added together have a rated thermal input of more than 20 megawatts. Cost-benefit analysis 3 An application to an enforcing authority under regulation 10 for a permit to operate a new installation, carrying out an activity with a total net thermal input exceeding 20 megawatts and generating electricity must be accompanied by a cost-benefit analysis that assesses the costs and benefits of operating the installation or converting the installation to operate as a high-efficiency cogeneration installation. 4 An operator of an installation, carrying out an activity with a total net thermal input exceeding 20 megawatts and generating electricity must apply to the enforcing authority under regulation 19(2) for a variation of the conditions of his permit before undertaking a substantial refurbishment. 5 The application for a variation of the conditions of the permit required by paragraph 4 must be accompanied by a cost-benefit analysis that assesses the costs and benefits of operating the installation, or converting the installation to operate, as a high-efficiency cogeneration installation. 6 An application to an enforcing authority under regulation 10 for a permit to operate a new installation with a total net thermal input exceeding 20 megawatts, other than an installation falling within paragraph 3, and generating waste heat at a useful temperature level, must be accompanied by a cost-benefit analysis that assesses the cost and benefits of utilising the waste heat to satisfy economically justified demand, including through cogeneration, and of the connection of that installation to a district heating and cooling network. 7 An operator of an installation with a total net thermal input exceeding 20 megawatts, and generating waste heat at a useful temperature level must apply to the enforcing authority under regulation 19(2) for a variation of the conditions of his permit before undertaking a substantial refurbishment. 8 The application for a variation of the conditions of the permit required by paragraph 7 must be accompanied by a cost-benefit analysis that assesses the cost and benefits of utilising the waste heat to satisfy economically justified demand, including through cogeneration, and of the connection of that installation to a district heating and cooling network. 9 An application to an enforcing authority under regulation 10 for a permit to operate a new installation with a total net thermal input exceeding 20 megawatts which forms part of a new or existing district heating and cooling network must be accompanied by a cost-benefit analysis that assesses the cost and benefits of utilising the waste heat from nearby installations. 10 An operator of an installation with a total net thermal input exceeding 20 megawatts which forms part of an existing district heating or cooling network must apply to the enforcing authority under regulation 19(2) for a variation in the conditions of his permit before undertaking a substantial refurbishment. 11 The application for a variation in the conditions of the permit required by paragraph 10 must be accompanied by a cost-benefit analysis that assesses the cost and benefits of utilising the waste heat from nearby installations. 12 Paragraphs 3 to 11 shall not apply to— 1 peak load and back-up electricity generating installations for which the application states that operation under 1,500 operating hours per year as a rolling average over a period of five years is planned; or 2 installations that need to be located close to a geological storage site approved under Directive 2009/31/EC. 13 Where the exemption specified in paragraph 12(1) applies, the enforcing authority shall include, in the permit, conditions ensuring that the operating hours remain within the constraints specified in paragraph 12(1). 14 Paragraphs 6 to 11 shall not apply to individual installations: 1 which do not form part of a district cooling network; and 2 with any of the following— a available waste heat of 100 kilowatts or less; b available waste heat, i greater than 100 kilowatts as hot water or steam, where there is no hot water heat demand greater than 100 kilowatts within the search radius from the source installation as set out in the table below, located within the connection distance from the centre of the source installation; or ii greater than 500 kilowatts as steam, where there is no steam-based heat demand greater than 500 kilowatts and no water heat demand greater than 100 kilowatts within the search radius from the centre of the installation as set out in the table below, located within the connection distance from the centre of the source installation; c a heat demand of— i 100 kilowatts or less for hot water heat demands; or ii 500 kilowatts or less for steam-based heat demands; d a hot water heat demand greater than 100 kilowatts, with no source of available waste heat greater than 100 kilowatts within the search radius from the centre of the installation as set out in the Table, located within the connection distance from the centre of the demand installation; or e a steam-based heat demand greater than 500 kilowatts, with no source of steam-based waste heat greater than 500 kilowatts within the search radius from the centre of the installation as set out in the Table, located within the connection distance from the centre of the demand installation. Table
Installation typeThermal capacity (kilowatts (kW) and megawatts (MW))Search radius (km) (measured from centre of the installation)
Hot water demand>100kW and <3.9 MW0.0038 x H, where H = thermal capacity in kW
≥3.9MW15
Steam demand>500kW and <12.5 MW0.0012 x H, where H = thermal capacity in kW
≥12.5 MW15
Waste heat source (hot water or steam)>100kW and <3.9 MW0.0038 x H, where H = thermal capacity in kW
≥3.9MW15
15 For the purposes of paragraph 14, “connection distance” means— 1 in the case of a hot water heat link, the thermal capacity in kilowatts of the source or demand, whichever is smaller, multiplied by 0.0038; or 2 in the case of a steam heat link, the thermal capacity in kilowatts of the source or demand, whichever is smaller, multiplied by 0.0012, expressed in kilometres. 16 From 31st December 2015, when considering permit applications and applications for the variation of conditions, the enforcing authority shall take into account both the outcome of the cost-benefit analysis and the outcome of the United Kingdom’s comprehensive national assessment required by Article 14(1) of the Energy Efficiency Directive. 17 Subject to paragraph 19, where a cost-benefit analysis, required pursuant to paragraphs 3, 5, 6 or 8 shows that benefits exceed costs, the enforcing authority may only grant the permit or vary the conditions of the permit subject to the inclusion of appropriate conditions that will ensure the operation of the installation in a manner shown by that analysis to be cost beneficial. 18 Subject to paragraph 19, where a cost-benefit analysis required pursuant to paragraphs 9 or 11 shows that benefits exceed costs, the regulator may only grant the permit or vary the conditions of the permit subject to the inclusion of appropriate conditions that will ensure the operation of the installation, in conjunction with the utilisation of the waste heat from nearby installations, in a manner shown by that analysis to be cost beneficial. 19 Paragraphs 17 and 18 do not apply if, in individual cases, the enforcing authority decides that there are imperative reasons of law, ownership or finance for it not to apply. In such cases, within two months of its decision, the enforcing authority shall submit a reasoned notification of it to the Department. 20 The provisions of this Schedule apply to installations covered by the IED without prejudice to the requirements of that Directive.

law.title: Waste and Contaminated Land (Northern Ireland) Order

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14" NumberOfProvisions="8" xml:lang="en" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/body" NumberOfProvisions="8" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Amendment of the Waste and Contaminated Land (Northern Ireland) Order 1997</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2" id="regulation-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/1" id="regulation-2-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Waste and Contaminated Land (Northern Ireland) Order 1997 is amended in accordance with paragraphs (2) to (5).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/2" id="regulation-2-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In Article 2(2) (General interpretation), in the appropriate alphabetical order insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P2para><UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“bio-waste” means biodegradable garden and park waste, food and kitchen waste from households, restaurants, caterers and retail premises and comparable waste from food processing plants;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“food waste” means controlled waste that was at any time food intended for human consumption (even if of no nutritional value) and includes biodegradable waste produced as a consequence of the processing or preparation of food, but does not include drink;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“separate collection of food waste” means that food waste is presented for collection, and collected in a manner that ensures that food waste is kept separate from other waste;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3" id="regulation-2-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In Article 5 (Duty of care, <Abbreviation Expansion="et cetera" xml:lang="la">etc.</Abbreviation>, as respects waste)—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/a/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/a" id="regulation-2-3-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (1), after sub-paragraph (aa) insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P3>
<Pnumber>ab</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>to prevent any contravention by any other person of paragraph (2B), (2E) or (2F);</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>;</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/b/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/b" id="regulation-2-3-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>after paragraph (2A) insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>2B</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>It shall, from 1st April 2016, be the duty of any person who controls or manages a food business that produces controlled waste to take all such measures available as are reasonable in the circumstances to secure the separate collection of food waste produced by that food business.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2C</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The duty in paragraph (2B) does not apply to—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>food waste produced by a food business that produces less than 5 kilograms of food waste per week; or</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>food waste that includes catering waste that originates from means of transport operating internationally; or</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>food waste produced in the period beginning on 1st April 2016 and ending on 31st March 2017—</Text><P5>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P5para><Text>by Health and Social Care trusts (as established under Article 10 of the Health and Personal Social Services (Northern Ireland) Order 1991<FootnoteRef Ref="f00006"/>); or</Text></P5para>
</P5>
<P5>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P5para><Text>by a food business that produces 5 kilograms or more, and less than 50 kilograms of food waste per week.</Text></P5para>
</P5>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2D</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The duty in paragraph (2B) is deemed to be satisfied where—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>the food waste produced by the food business is recovered at the premises of the food business, and “recovery” in this paragraph has the same meaning as in the Waste Management Licensing Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2003<FootnoteRef Ref="f00007"/>; or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>the food waste is mixed with other bio-waste to the extent that the resultant mixed waste is presented for collection in a manner that ensures that the amount of food waste collected is not substantially less than would be the case were the wastes not mixed.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2E</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>It shall, from 1st April 2015, be the duty of any person who transports controlled waste to collect and transport separately from other waste any waste presented for collection—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in accordance with paragraph (2B);</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>in a receptacle provided in accordance with Article 20A(3).</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2F</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>It shall, from 1st April 2017, be the duty of any person who produces food waste (other than an occupier of a domestic property as respects the household waste produced on that property) to ensure that food waste is not deposited in a lateral drain or public sewer, or in a drain or sewer that connects to a lateral drain or public sewer.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>;</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/c/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/c" id="regulation-2-3-c">
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (7), for “the duty imposed by paragraph (1)” substitute “a duty imposed by paragraphs (1), (2B), (2E) or (2F)”;</Text>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/d/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/d" id="regulation-2-3-d">
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (8)—</Text>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/d/i/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/d/i" id="regulation-2-3-d-i">
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>after “fails” insert “without reasonable excuse”; and</Text>
</P4para></P4>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/d/ii/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/d/ii" id="regulation-2-3-d-ii">
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>for “paragraph (1) or paragraph (2A)” substitute “paragraphs (1), (2A), (2B), (2E) or (2F)”;</Text>
</P4para></P4>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/e/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/e" id="regulation-2-3-e">
<Pnumber>e</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (9), for “the duty imposed on them by paragraph (1)” substitute “a duty imposed on them by paragraphs (1), (2B), (2E) or (2F)”;</Text>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/f/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/3/f" id="regulation-2-3-f">
<Pnumber>f</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>after paragraph (13), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>14</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>In this Article—</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“business” includes the undertaking of a canteen, club, school, hospital or institution, whether carried on for profit or not, and any undertaking or activity carried on by a district council;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“catering waste” means all waste food, including used cooking oil, originating in restaurants, catering facilities and kitchens, including central kitchens and household kitchens;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“drain”, “lateral drain”, “public sewer” and “sewer” have the same meanings as in Article 2 of the Water and Sewerage Services (Northern Ireland) Order 2006<FootnoteRef Ref="f00008"/>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“food business” means an undertaking, whether carried on for profit or not, and whether public or private, carrying out any activity related to the processing, distribution, preparation or sale of food.</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4" id="regulation-2-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In Article 20 (Collection of controlled waste)—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/a/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/a" id="regulation-2-4-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (1)—</Text>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/a/i/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/a/i" id="regulation-2-4-a-i">
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>at the end of sub-paragraph (a), omit “and”; and</Text>
</P4para></P4>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/a/ii/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/a/ii" id="regulation-2-4-a-ii">
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>at the end of sub-paragraph (b), omit “.” and insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P3para><Text>; and</Text>
</P3para>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>if requested by the occupier of premises in its district to collect any food waste from the premises presented for collection in accordance with Article 5(2B), to arrange for the collection of the food waste.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>;</AppendText>
</P4para></P4>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/b/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/4/b" id="regulation-2-4-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>after paragraph (1), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>1A</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>In sub-paragraph (1)(c), the reference to “food waste” does not include waste from an occupier of a domestic property as respects the household waste produced on the property.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/14/regulation/2/5" id="regulation-2-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After Article 20 (Collection of controlled waste) insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="secondary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P1group>
<Title>Separate collection of food waste</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">20A</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2>
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>This Article applies when a district council is making an arrangement in accordance with Article 20(1)(a).</Text></P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>A district council shall, from 1st April 2015, take such steps as the council considers reasonable to promote separate collection of food waste (including the making of arrangements for the provision of a receptacle which enables the separate collection of food waste from every domestic property in its area).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>A district council shall, from 1st April 2017, arrange for there to be provided to the occupier of every domestic property in its area—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>a receptacle which enables the separate collection of food waste from the property; or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>where a district council is satisfied that the amount of food waste that will be collected is not substantially less than would be collected in a receptacle provided under paragraph (a), a receptacle which enables the occupier to present food waste and other bio-waste for separate collection.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>In this Article—</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“domestic property” means a building or self-contained part of a building which is used wholly for the purposes of living accommodation;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“receptacle” has the same meaning as in Article 21(10).</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>
