http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1972/28/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1972/28/body" NumberOfProvisions="11"><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1972/28/crossheading/amendments-of-factories-act-1961" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1972/28/crossheading/amendments-of-factories-act-1961" NumberOfProvisions="9" id="crossheading-amendments-of-factories-act-1961"><Title> Amendments of Factories Act 1961</Title><P1group><Title> Medical examinations of persons employed in factories. <CommentaryRef Ref="c822781"/></Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1972/28/section/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1972/28/section/3" id="section-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><Text>The Factories Act 1961 shall have effect as if the following section were inserted after section 10 thereof:—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P1group Layout="below"><Title/><P1><Pnumber PuncAfter="">10A</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>If an employment medical adviser is of opinion that ther ought, on grounds mentioned in subsection (2) below, to be a medical examination of a person or persons employed in a factory, he may serve on the occupier of the factory a written notice stating that he is of that opinion and requiring that the occupier shall permit a medical examination in accordance with this section of the person or persons in question, and the examination shall be permitted accordingly.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The grounds on which a medical examination of a person may be required by an employment medical adviser’s notice under subsection (1) above are that (in the adviser’s opinion) the persons health has been or is being injured, or it is possible that it has been, is being or will be injured, by reason of the nature of the work he is or has been called upon to do or may (to the adviser’s knowledge) be called upon to do ; and a notice under that subsection may be given with respect to one or more named persons or to persons of a class or description specified in the notice.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A notice under subsection (1) above shall name the place where the medical examination is to be conducted and, if it is a place other than the factory, the day on which and the time at which it is to be begun ; and—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>every person to whom the notice relates shall be informed, as soon as practicable after service thereof, of the contents thereof and of the fact that he is free to attend for the purpose of submitting to the examination ; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>if the notice states that the examination is to be conducted at the factory, suitable accomodation therat shall be provided for the conduct of the examination.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A medical examination conducted in pursuance of a notice under subsection (1) above shall be begun within seven days after the day on which the notice is served, and shall be conducted by, or in accordance with arrangements made by, an employment medical adviser, and take place at a reasonable time during working hours.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>An employment medical adviser may, by written notice served on the occupier of a factory, cancel a notice served on the occupier under subsection (1) above ; and a notice which relates to two or more named persons may be cancelled either in relation to them all or in relation to any one or more of them.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this section “ medical examination” includes pathological, physiological and radiological tests and similar investigations.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></BlockAmendment></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/36" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1974/36" NumberOfProvisions="3" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/36/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1974/36/body" NumberOfProvisions="3"><P1group><Title> Amendment of paragraph 1 of the Table to section 1 of theMines(Working Facilities and Support) Act 1966 <CommentaryRef Ref="c705679"/></Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/36/section/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1974/36/section/1" id="section-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P1para><Text>The following paragraph shall be substituted for paragraph 1 of theTable to section 1 of the Mines (Working Facilities and Support) Act 1966:—</Text><BlockText><Text>

					‘‘ TABLE Paragraph 1 of Table.</Text></BlockText><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/36/section/1/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1974/36/section/1/1" id="section-1-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>This paragraph applies to any minerals other than coal and peat cut for purposes other than sale.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/36/section/1/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1974/36/section/1/2" id="section-1-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A right to search for or work any minerals to which this paragraph applies may be conferred on any person (exercisable either by himself or through a lessee).</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/36/section/1/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1974/36/section/1/3" id="section-1-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where the working of any minerals to which this paragraph applies, orthe working of any such minerals in the most efficient and economical manner, is impeded by any restrictions, terms or conditions contained in a mining lease, or otherwise binding on the person entitled to work the minerals, a right may be conferred to work the minerals freed wholly or partially from the restrictions or conditions, or to work the minerals on other terms and conditions.’’</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Body></Primary></Legislation>

Part IV Information about atmospheric pollution Research and publicity.791A local authority may—aundertake, or contribute towards the cost of, investigation and research relevant to the problem of air pollution; andbArrange for the publication of information on that problem.2Without prejudice to the generality of the preceding subsection, local authorities may obtain information about the emission of pollutants and other substances into the air—aby issuing notices under the following section; andbby measuring and recording the emissions, and for that purpose entering on any premises, whether by agreement or in exercise of the power conferred by section 91 of this Act; andcby entering into arrangements with occupiers of premises under which they measure and record emissions on behalf of the local authority;but references to premises in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this subsection do not include private dwellings.3A local authority shall not be entitled to exercise the power mentioned in paragraph (b) of the preceding subsection for the purpose of measuring and recording such emissions on any premises unless—athe authority has given to the occupier of the premises a notice—ispecifying the kind of emissions in question and the steps it proposes to take on the premises for the purpose of measuring and recording emissions of that kind, andiistating that it proposes to exercise that power for that purpose unless the occupier makes a request to the authority in pursuance of the following provisions of this subsection; andbthe period of twenty-one days beginning with the day on which the notice was given has expired,and shall not be entitled to exercise that power in consequence of the notice if during that period the occupier gives a notice to the authority requesting it to serve on him a notice under the following section with respect to the emissions.4Nothing in this section shall authorise a local authority to investigate emissions from any process subject to Part I of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 orwork subject to the Alkali Act otherwise than by issuing notices under the following section, or by exercising the powers conferred on the authority by subsection (1)(a) of this section without entering the work.5In acting under subsection (1)(b) of this section, a local authority shall ensure that the material published is presented in such a way that no information relating to a trade secret is disclosed, except with the consent in writing of a person authorised to disclose it . . . 6Breach of a duty imposed by the preceding subsection shall be actionable; but in any proceedings, whether civil or criminal, brought against a local authority, or any member or officer of a local authority, on the grounds that any information has been published, it shall be a defence to show that it was published in compliance with the preceding provisions of this section.7The preceding subsection applies in particular to any proceedings brought under section 26 of the Clean Air Act 1956 (which, as amended by subsection (10) of this section, makes it an offence to disclose information relating to any trade secret).8So long as a local authority exercises any of its powers under subsection (2) of this section, it shall from time to time consult such persons carrying on any trade or business in the authority’s area, or such organisations appearing to the authority to be representative of those persons, and such persons appearing to the authority to be conversant with problems of air pollution or to have an interest in local amenity as appear to the authority to be appropriate—aAbout the way in which the local authority exercises its powers under this and the following section; andbAbout the extent to which, and the manner in which, any information collected under those powers should be made available to the public.9The consultations shall take place from time to time as the authority think necessary, but not less than twice in each financial year.10Paragraphs (a) and (b) of section 25 of the Clean Air Act 1956 (which are superseded by the provisions of this section) shall cease to have effect, and in paragraph (c) of that section for the words “that problem” there shall be substituted the words “the problem of the pollution of the air”; and in section 26 of that Act (which relates to the unjustified disclosure of information relating to any manufacturing process or trade secret) the words “manufacturing process or” shall cease to have effect.

DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1975/74/section/48/3/c" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1975/74/section/48/3/c" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1975/74/section/48/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1975/74/section/48/5" id="section-48-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without and that subsection shall apply to Greater London as if it were a county with the like omissions and as if that duty were imposed jointly on the councils of the London boroughs and the Common Council of the City of London.</Text></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1985/51/schedule/6/paragraph/5/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1985/51/schedule/6/paragraph/5/2" id="schedule-6-paragraph-5-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In section 6(1) of that Act after the words “A county council” there shall be inserted the words “and a metropolitan district council”.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43" NumberOfProvisions="102" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2024-10-14"><Primary><Schedules RestrictStartDate="2021-07-16"><Title> SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3" NumberOfProvisions="9" id="schedule-3"><Number>SCHEDULE 3</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Amendments of Part I of the Health and Safety at Work <Abbreviation Expansion="et cetera" xml:lang="la">etc.</Abbreviation> Act 1974</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/1" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Section 6 (general duties of manufacturers etc. as regard articles and substances for use at work) shall be amended as follows.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/2" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For subsection (1)

					(general duties of designers, manufacturers, importers and suppliers of articles for use at work) there shall be substituted the following subsections—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="order" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>It shall be the duty of any person who designs, manufactures, imports or supplies any article for use at work or any article of fairground equipment—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that the article is so designed and constructed that it will be safe and without risks to health at all times when it is being set, used, cleaned or maintained by a person at work;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to carry out or arrange for the carrying out of such testing and examination as may be necessary for the performance of the duty imposed on him by the preceding paragraph;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to take such steps as are necessary to secure that persons supplied by that person with the article are provided with adequate information about the use for which the article is designed or has been tested and about any conditions necessary to ensure that it will be safe and without risks to health at all such times as are mentioned in paragraph (a) above and when it is being dismantled or disposed of; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to take such steps as are necessary to secure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that persons so supplied are provided with all such revisions of information provided to them by virtue of the preceding paragraph as are necessary by reason of its becoming known that anything gives rise to a serious risk to health or safety.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>1A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>It shall be the duty of any person who designs, manufactures, imports or supplies any article of fairground equipment—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that the article is so designed and constructed that it will be safe and without risks to health at all times when it is being used for or in connection with the entertainment of members of the public;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to carry out or arrange for the carrying out of such testing and examination as may be necessary for the performance of the duty imposed on him by the preceding paragraph;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to take such steps as are necessary to secure that persons supplied by that person with the article are provided with adequate information about the use for which the article is designed or has been tested and about any conditions necessary to ensure that it will be safe and without risks to health at all times when it is being used for or in connection with the entertainment of members of the public; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to take such steps as are necessary to secure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that persons so supplied are provided with all such revisions of information provided to them by virtue of the preceding paragraph as are necessary by reason of its becoming known that anything gives rise to a serious risk to health or safety.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/3" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (2)

					(duty of person who undertakes the design or manufacture of an article for use at work to carry out research), after the word 

						“work” there shall be inserted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                  

						“or of any article of fairground equipment
                ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/4" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (3)

					(duty of persons who erect or install articles for use at work)—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/4/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/4/a" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-4-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>after the words 

								“persons at work” there shall be inserted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                      

								“or who erects or installs any article of fairground equipment
                    ”</InlineAmendment>; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/4/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/4/b" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-4-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the words from 

								“it is” onwards there shall be substituted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                      

								“the article is erected or installed makes it unsafe or a risk to health at any such time as is mentioned in paragraph (a) of subsection (1) or, as the case may be, in paragraph (a) of subsection (1) or (1A) above.
                    ”</InlineAmendment></Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/5" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For subsection (4)

					(general duties of manufacturers, importers and suppliers of substances for use at work) there shall be substituted the following subsection—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>It shall be the duty of any person who manufactures, imports or supplies any substance—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that the substance will be safe and without risks to health at all times when it is being used, handled, processed, stored or transported by a person at work or in premises to which section 4 above applies;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to carry out or arrange for the carrying out of such testing and examination as may be necessary for the performance of the duty imposed on him by the preceding paragraph;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to take such steps as are necessary to secure that persons supplied by that person with the substance are provided with adequate information about any risks to health or safety to which the inherent properties of the substance may give rise, about the results of any relevant tests which have been carried out on or in connection with the substance and about any conditions necessary to ensure that the substance will be safe and without risks to health at all such times as are mentioned in paragraph (a) above and when the substance is being disposed of; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to take such steps as are necessary to secure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that persons so supplied are provided with all such revisions of information provided to them by virtue of the preceding paragraph as are necessary by reason of its becoming known that anything gives rise to a serious risk to health or safety.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/6" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/6" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-6"><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (5)

					(duty of person who undertakes the manufacture of a substance for use at work to carry out research)—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/6/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/6/a" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-6-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the words 

								“substance for use at work” there shall be substituted the word <InlineAmendment>“
                      

								“substance
                    ”</InlineAmendment>; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/6/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/6/b" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-6-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>at the end there shall be inserted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                      

								“at all such times as are mentioned in paragraph (a) of subsection (4) above
                    ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-7"><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (8)

					(relief from duties for persons relying on undertakings by others)—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7/a" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-7-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the words 

								“for or to another” there shall be substituted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                      

								“for use at work or an article of fairground equipment and does so for or to another
                    ”</InlineAmendment>;</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7/b" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-7-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the words 

								“when properly used” there shall be substituted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                      

								“at all such times as are mentioned in paragraph (a) of subsection (1) or, as the case may be, in paragraph (a) of subsection (1) or (1A) above
                    ”</InlineAmendment>; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7/c" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/7/c" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-7-c"><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the words 

								“by subsection (1)(a) above” there shall be substituted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                      

								“by virtue of that paragraph
                    ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/8" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/8" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-8"><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After the said subsection (8) there shall be inserted the following subsection—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>8A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Nothing in subsection (7) or (8) above shall relieve any person who imports any article or substance from any duty in respect of anything which—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>in the case of an article designed outside the United Kingdom, was done by and in the course of any trade, profession or other undertaking carried on by, or was within the control of, the person who designed the article; or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>in the case of an article or substance manufactured outside the United Kingdom, was done by and in the course of any trade, profession or other undertaking carried on by, or was within the control of, the person who manufactured the article or substance.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/9" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/9" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-9"><Pnumber>9</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (9)

					(definition of supplier in certain cases of supply under a hire-purchase agreement), for the words 

						“article for use at work or substance for use at work” there shall be substituted the words <InlineAmendment>“
                  

						“article or substance
                ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/10" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1987/43/schedule/3/paragraph/1/10" id="schedule-3-paragraph-1-10"><Pnumber>10</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For subsection (10)

					(meaning of 

						“properly used”) there shall be substituted the following subsection—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>10</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For the purposes of this section an absence of safety or a risk to health shall be disregarded in so far as the case in or in relation to which it would arise is shown to be one the occurrence of which could not reasonably be foreseen; and in determining whether any duty imposed by virtue of paragraph (a) of subsection (1), (1A) or (4) above has been performed regard shall be had to any relevant information or advice which has been provided to any person by the person by whom the article has been designed, manufactured, imported or supplied or, as the case may be, by the person by whom the substance has been manufactured, imported or supplied.</Text></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43" NumberOfProvisions="402" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Primary xmlns:leg="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation"><Schedules><Title>SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15" NumberOfProvisions="35" NumberFormat="default" id="schedule-15"><Number>SCHEDULE 15</Number><TitleBlock>
<Title>Consequential and Minor Amendments of Enactments</Title>
</TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air" NumberOfProvisions="1" id="schedule-15-crossheading-workplace-emissions-into-the-air"><Title>Workplace emissions into the air</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14">
<Pnumber>14</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>Section 5 of the <MarginNoteRef Ref="m00160"/>Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 (general duty in relation to harmful emissions into the air from prescribed premises) shall be amended by the insertion—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/a/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/a" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in subsection (1), at the beginning, of the words “Subject to subsection (5) below,”; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/b/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/b" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>after subsection (4), of the following subsections—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" TargetClass="primary" Context="main" Format="default" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The foregoing provisions of this section shall not apply in relation to any process which is a prescribed process as from the date which is the determination date for that process.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>For the purposes of subsection (6) above, the “determination date” for a prescribed process is—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in the case of a process for which an authorisation is granted, the date on which the enforcing authority grants it, whether in pursuance of the application or, on an appeal, of a direction to grant it;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in the case of a process for which an authorisation is refused, the date of the refusal or, on an appeal, of the affirmation of the refusal.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In subsections (5) and (6) above “authorisation”, “enforcing authority” and “prescribed process” have the meaning given in section 1 of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and the reference to an appeal is a reference to an appeal under section 15 of that Act.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P1para>
</P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

id="schedule-9-paragraph-10-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After section 7 of that Act (imposition of restrictions on the working of minerals where a person having an interest in land is not entitled to support or to sufficient support for buildings or works) there shall be inserted the following section—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P1group><Title> Special provisions applying to section 7.</Title><P1><Pnumber>7A</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subject to subsections (2) and (3) below, on an application under section 7 of this Act, the applicant shall not be required to pay or give any compensation or consideration in respect of the imposition of restrictions appearing to the court to be justified by the existence of any right to withdraw support to which any person is entitled under section 38 of the Coal Industry Act 1994 (withdrawal of support).</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subsection (1) above shall not apply in a case where, in accordance with subsection (2)(b) of section 38 of the Coal Industry Act 1994, that section applies to the land in question by virtue of subsection (5)(a) of section 2 of the Coal Industry Act 1975.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subsection (1) above shall apply in any case where section 38 of the Coal Industry Act 1994 applies to the land in question otherwise than by virtue of subsection (5) of section 2 of the Coal Industry Act 1975 only if the application under section 7 of this Act is sent to the Secretary of State before the end of the period of six months beginning with the date on which particulars of the notice relating to the land to which the application relates are first registered by the Coal Authority under section 56 of the Coal Industry Act 1994.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Notwithstanding anything in section 12 of this Act, any restrictions the imposition of which appears to the court to be justified as mentioned in subsection (1) above—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may be imposed under section 7 of this Act on the application of, and so as to vest the right to enforce the restrictions in, any such company, authority or body as is mentioned in the said section 12; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may be so imposed on the application of, and so as to vest the right to enforce the restrictions in—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the National Rivers Authority or any water or sewerage undertaker;</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>any public gas supplier within the meaning of Part I of the Gas Act 1986; or</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>iii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>any company or other body or person carrying on an undertaking primarily for the supply of electricity or hydraulic power for public purposes or to members of the public.</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

RestrictStartDate="2014-04-22"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/body" NumberOfProvisions="11" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="1995-01-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/crossheading/marine-pollution" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/crossheading/marine-pollution" NumberOfProvisions="8" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." id="crossheading-marine-pollution" RestrictStartDate="1995-01-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Title> Marine Pollution</Title><P1group RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Status="Dead" ConfersPower="true" Match="false"><Title> Liability and compensation for oil pollution damage: 1992 Protocols.</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5" id="section-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/1" id="section-5-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For the purpose of enabling effect to be given to the 1992 Protocols, the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340821"/>Merchant Shipping (Oil Pollution) Act 1971 and the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340831"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1974 shall have effect subject to the amendments contained in Parts I and II respectively of Schedule 4 to the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340841"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1988 with the substitution, in the definition in section 19(1) of the1971 Act of “the Convention” and in the definitions in section 1(1) of the1974 Act of “the Liability Convention” and “the Fund Convention”, of “1992” for “1984”.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2" id="section-5-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Accordingly—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/a" id="section-5-2-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the word “<Term id="term-1984">1984</Term>” shall be omitted from the section 4A(1) of the 1974 Act and the paragraph 4(a) and (d) constituting Schedule 1 to the 1974 Act as respectively inserted and substituted by Part II of Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/b" id="section-5-2-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>paragraph 18 of Schedule 4 to the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340851"/>Merchant Shipping (Registration, <Abbreviation Expansion="et cetera" xml:lang="la">etc.</Abbreviation>) Act 1993 (which provides that section 34 of and Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act shall not have effect) is hereby repealed and the entry for Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act shall be deemed not to have been included in Part II of Schedule 5 to the 1993 Act (pre-consolidation repeals).</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3" id="section-5-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Her Majesty may by Order in Council make such provision as appears to Her Majesty to be appropriate i n connection with the implementation of any transitional provisions contained in the 1992 Protocols or the Conventions which they amend; and any such Order may in particular provide, in relation to occurrences of any description specified in the Order—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a" id="section-5-3-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for provisions of the1971 Act or the1974 Act to have effect—</Text><P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/i" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/i" id="section-5-3-a-i"><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>to such extent as is so specified, as if Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act were not in force, and</Text></P4para></P4><P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/ii" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/ii" id="section-5-3-a-ii"><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>to such extent as is so specified, as if that Schedule were in force;</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/b" id="section-5-3-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for any such provisions to have effect (whether as amended by that Schedule or not) subject to such modifications as are so specified.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4" id="section-5-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this section “<Term id="term-the-1992-protocols">the 1992 Protocols</Term>” means—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/a" id="section-5-4-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the Protocol of 1992 to amend the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage 1969 signed in London on 27th November 1992; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/b" id="section-5-4-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the Protocol of 1992 to amend the International Convention on the Establishment of an International Fund for Compensation for Oil Pollution Damage 1971 signed in London on 27th November 1992.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

RestrictStartDate="2014-04-22"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/body" NumberOfProvisions="11" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="1995-01-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/crossheading/marine-pollution" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/crossheading/marine-pollution" NumberOfProvisions="8" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." id="crossheading-marine-pollution" RestrictStartDate="1995-01-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Title> Marine Pollution</Title><P1group RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="1994-10-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Title> Extension of rights of Fund by subrogation.</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7" id="section-7"><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1" id="section-7-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In section 8 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340891"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1974 (Acquisition by International Fund of rights of recipients of payments made by the Fund in cases of oil pollution damage)—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/a" id="section-7-1-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for subsection (1), there shall be inserted the following subsection—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text> In respect of any sum paid by the Fund as compensation for pollution damage the Fund shall acquire by subrogation any rights in respect of the damage which the recipient has (or but for the payment would have) against any other person,</Text></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment><AppendText>; and</AppendText></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/b" id="section-7-1-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>subsection (3) shall be omitted.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/2" id="section-7-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The amendments made by subsection (1) above apply in relation to payments made by the Fund after this section comes into force.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28" NumberOfProvisions="78" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2014-04-22"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/body" NumberOfProvisions="11" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="1995-01-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/crossheading/marine-pollution" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/crossheading/marine-pollution" NumberOfProvisions="8" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." id="crossheading-marine-pollution" RestrictStartDate="1995-01-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Title> Marine Pollution</Title><P1group RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="1994-07-28" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Title> Amendments as to powers of implementation.</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3" id="section-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/1" id="section-3-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Section 20 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1979 (power by Order in Council to implement international conventions relating to pollution from ships, etc) shall be amended as follows.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/2" id="section-3-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (3)(a), in the list of enactments there specified, after the entry for the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340801"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1970, there shall be inserted the following entry— <InlineAmendment>“
              section 33 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1988 (which relates to investigations of marine accidents);
            ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/3" id="section-3-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (4), after paragraph (a), there shall be inserted the following paragraph—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P3><Pnumber>aa</Pnumber><P3para><Text>make provision in terms of any document which the Secretary of State or any person considers relevant from time to time;</Text></P3para></P3></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/4" id="section-3-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After subsection (4), there shall be inserted the following subsections—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>4A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an Order in Council under subsection (1) of this section authorises the making of regulations for the purpose of giving effect to an agreement mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (cc) or falling within paragraph (d) of that subsection the Order also authorises the making of regulations for the purpose of giving effect to an agreement which provides for the modification of such an agreement.</Text></P2para><P2para><Text>This subsection applies in relation to Orders in Council and international agreements whenever made.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4B</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations made by virtue of paragraph (e) of subsection (4) of this section—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may make provision corresponding to the provision authorised for an Order by paragraphs (a) to (d) of subsection (4) of this section; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>shall be subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of either House of Parliament.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

              section 33 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1988 (which relates to investigations of marine accidents);
            ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/3" id="section-3-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (4), after paragraph (a), there shall be inserted the following paragraph—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P3><Pnumber>aa</Pnumber><P3para><Text>make provision in terms of any document which the Secretary of State or any person considers relevant from time to time;</Text></P3para></P3></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/4" id="section-3-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After subsection (4), there shall be inserted the following subsections—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>4A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an Order in Council under subsection (1) of this section authorises the making of regulations for the purpose of giving effect to an agreement mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (cc) or falling within paragraph (d) of that subsection the Order also authorises the making of regulations for the purpose of giving effect to an agreement which provides for the modification of such an agreement.</Text></P2para><P2para><Text>This subsection applies in relation to Orders in Council and international agreements whenever made.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4B</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations made by virtue of paragraph (e) of subsection (4) of this section—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may make provision corresponding to the provision authorised for an Order by paragraphs (a) to (d) of subsection (4) of this section; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>shall be subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of either House of Parliament.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

                  ”</Repeal></InlineAmendment></Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25/schedule/22/paragraph/57/6" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25/schedule/22/paragraph/57/6" id="schedule-22-paragraph-57-6"><Pnumber><Repeal ChangeId="key-0aa53a-1595948373335" CommentaryRef="key-0aa53a" RetainText="true">6</Repeal></Pnumber><P2para><Text><Repeal ChangeId="key-0aa53a-1595948373335" CommentaryRef="key-0aa53a" RetainText="true">Subsection (9) (duty to furnish the National Rivers Authority with information for purposes of its register) shall cease to have effect.</Repeal></Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

the 1974 act.title: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974

xmls: <Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25" NumberOfProvisions="809" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2026-07-16"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25/body" NumberOfProvisions="215" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2026-07-16"><Part DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25/part/V" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25/part/V" NumberOfProvisions="66" id="part-V" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2026-07-16"><Number>Part V</Number><Title> Miscellaneous, General and Supplemental Provisions</Title><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25/part/V/crossheading/waste" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25/part/V/crossheading/waste" NumberOfProvisions="8" id="part-V-crossheading-waste" RestrictExtent="E+W+S" RestrictStartDate="2023-12-26"><Title> Waste</Title><P1group RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01"><Title> National waste strategy.</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25/section/92" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25/section/92" id="section-92"><Pnumber>92</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25/section/92/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25/section/92/1" id="section-92-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Before section 45 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539641"/>Environmental Protection Act 1990 there shall be inserted—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" Format="default"><P1group><Title> National waste strategy: England and Wales.</Title><P1><Pnumber>44A</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The Secretary of State shall as soon as possible prepare a statement (“<Term>the strategy</Term>”) containing his policies in relation to the recovery and disposal of waste in England and Wales.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The strategy shall consist of or include—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>a statement which relates to the whole of England and Wales; or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>two or more statements which between them relate to the whole of England and Wales.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The Secretary of State may from time to time modify the strategy.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without prejudice to the generality of what may be included in the strategy, the strategy must include—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>a statement of the Secretary of State’s policies for attaining the objectives specified in Schedule 2A to this Act;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>provisions relating to each of the following, that is to say—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the type, quantity and origin of waste to be recovered or disposed of;</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>general technical requirements; and</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>iii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>any special requirements for particular wastes.</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In preparing the strategy or any modification of it, the Secretary of State—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>shall consult the Environment Agency,</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>shall consult—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>such bodies or persons appearing to him to be representative of the interests of local government, and</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>such bodies or persons appearing to him to be representative of the interests of industry,</Text></P4para></P4><Text>as he may consider appropriate, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may consult such other bodies or persons as he considers appropriate.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without prejudice to any power to give directions conferred by section 40 of the Environment Act 1995, the Secretary of State may give directions to the Environment Agency requiring it—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to advise him on the policies which are to be included in the strategy;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to carry out a survey of or investigation into—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the kinds or quantities of waste which it appears to that Agency is likely to be situated in England and Wales,</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the facilities which are or appear to that Agency likely to be available or needed in England and Wales for recovering or disposing of any such waste,</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>iii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>any other matter upon which the Secretary of State wishes to be informed in connection with his preparation of the strategy or any modification of it,</Text></P4para></P4><Text>and to report its findings to him.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A direction under subsection (6)(b) above—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>shall specify or describe the matters or the areas which are to be the subject of the survey or investigation; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may make provision in relation to the manner in which—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the survey or investigation is to be carried out, or</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the findings are to be reported or made available to other persons.</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where a direction is given under subsection (6)(b) above, the Environment Agency shall, in accordance with any requirement of the direction,—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>before carrying out the survey or investigation, consult—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>such bodies or persons appearing to it to be representative of local planning authorities, and</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>such bodies or persons appearing to it to be representative of the interests of industry,</Text></P4para></P4><Text>as it may consider appropriate; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>make its findings available to those authorities.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>9</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this section—</Text><UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition"><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>local planning authority</Term>” has the same meaning as in the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539651"/>Town and Country Planning Act 1990;</Text></Para></ListItem><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>strategy</Term>” includes the strategy as modified from time to time and “<Term>statement</Term>” shall be construed accordingly.</Text></Para></ListItem></UnorderedList></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>10</Pnumber><P2para><Text>This section makes provision for the purpose of implementing Article 7 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539661"/>directive of the Council of the European Communities, dated 15th July 1975, on waste, as amended by—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539671"/>directive of that Council, dated 18th March 1991, amending directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1975/0442" id="c00001" Class="EuropeanEconomicCommunityDirective" Year="1975" Number="442">75/442/<Acronym Expansion="European Economic Community">EEC</Acronym></Citation> on waste; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539681"/>directive of that Council, dated 23rd December 1991, standardising and rationalising reports on the implementation of certain Directives relating to the environment.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group><P1group><Title> National waste strategy: Scotland.</Title><P1><Pnumber>44B</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>SEPA shall as soon as possible prepare a statement (“<Term>the strategy</Term>”) containing its policies in relation to the recovery and disposal of waste in Scotland.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>SEPA may from time to time modify the strategy.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without prejudice to the generality of what may be included in the strategy, the strategy must include—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>a statement of SEPA’s policies for attaining the objectives specified in Schedule 2A to this Act;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>provisions relating to each of the following, that is to say—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the type, quantity and origin of waste to be recovered or disposed of;</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>general technical requirements; and</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>iii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>any special requirements for particular wastes.</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In preparing the strategy or any modification of it SEPA shall consult—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>such bodies or persons appearing to it to be representative of the interests of industry as it may consider appropriate;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>such local authorities as appear to it to be likely to be affected by the strategy or modification,</Text></P3para></P3><Text>and may consult such other bodies or persons as it considers appropriate.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without prejudice to any power to give directions conferred by section 40 of the Environment Act 1995, the Secretary of State may give directions to SEPA—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>as to the policies which are to be included in the strategy;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>requiring it to carry out a survey or investigation into—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the kinds or quantities of waste which it appears to it is likely to be situated in Scotland,</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the facilities which are or appear to it likely to be available or needed in Scotland for recovering or disposing of any such waste,</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>iii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>any other matter which the Secretary of State considers appropriate in connection with its preparation of the strategy or any modifications of it.</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A direction under subsection (5)(b) above—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>shall specify or describe the matters or the areas which are to be the subject of the survey or investigation; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may make provision in relation to the manner in which—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the survey or investigation is to be carried out, or</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the findings are to be reported or made available to other persons.</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where a direction is given under subsection (5)(b) above SEPA shall, in accordance with any requirement of the direction—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>before carrying out the survey or investigation, consult—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>such bodies or persons appearing to it to be representative of planning authorities, and</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>such bodies or persons appearing to it to be representative of the interests of industry,</Text></P4para></P4><Text>as it may consider appropriate; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>make its findings available to those authorities.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this section—</Text><UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition"><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>planning authority</Term>” means an authority within the meaning of section 172 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539691"/>Local Government (Scotland) Act 1973;</Text></Para></ListItem><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>strategy</Term>” includes the strategy as modified from time to time and “<Term>statement</Term>” shall be construed accordingly.</Text></Para></ListItem></UnorderedList></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>9</Pnumber><P2para><Text>This section makes provision for the purpose of implementing Article 7 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539701"/>directive of the Council of the European Communities dated 15th July 1975 on waste, as amended by—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539711"/>directive of that Council dated 18th March 1991 amending directive <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1975/0442" id="c00002" Class="EuropeanEconomicCommunityDirective" Year="1975" Number="442">75/442/EEC</Citation> on waste; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the <CommentaryRef Ref="c14539721"/>directive of that Council dated 23rd December 1991 standardising and rationalising reports on the implementation of certain Directives relating to the environment.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25/section/92/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/25/section/92/2" id="section-92-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After Schedule 2 to that Act there shall be inserted the Schedule set out in Schedule 12 to this Act.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Part></Body></Primary></Legislation>

law.title: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act

xmls: <Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40" NumberOfProvisions="140" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2020-12-31"><Primary><Schedules RestrictStartDate="2020-12-31"><Title> SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1" NumberOfProvisions="12" id="schedule-1" RestrictExtent="S" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01"><Number>SCHEDULE 1</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Setting and alteration of certain penalties</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/crossheading/increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/crossheading/increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences" NumberOfProvisions="1" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01" id="schedule-1-crossheading-increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences"><Title> Increase of fines for certain summary offences</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01" BlanketAmendment="true" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/1" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The enactments specified in column 2 of Part II of Schedule 2 to this Act, which relate to the maximum fines for the offences mentioned (and broadly described) in column 1 of that Schedule, shall have effect as if the maximum fine that may be imposed on summary conviction of any offence so mentioned were a fine not exceeding the amount specified in column 4 of that Schedule instead of a fine not exceeding the amount specified in column 3 of that Schedule (being the amount of the maximum fine in respect of the offence immediately before the passing of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8315571"/>Criminal Law Act 1977), but this sub-paragraph shall not alter the maximum daily fine, if any, provided for by any of those enactments.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/2" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In section 203 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8315581"/>Local Government (Scotland) Act 1973 (offences against byelaws), except as applied to byelaws made under any provision contained in a local or private Act other than by a local authority, for any reference to £20 there shall be substituted a reference to £50.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subject to sub-paragraph (4) below, this sub-paragraph applies to any pre-1949 enactment however framed or worded which—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>as regards any summary offence makes a person liable on conviction thereof to a fine of, or not exceeding, a specified amount less than £50 which has not been altered since the end of 1948 (and is not altered by this Act); or</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>confers power by subordinate instrument to make a person, as regards any summary offence (whether or not created by the instrument), liable on conviction thereof to a fine of, or a maximum fine of, less than £50 which has not been altered since the end of 1948 (and is not altered by this Act).</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/4" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Sub-paragraph (3) above does not apply to any offence to which section 292(2)(b) of the Principal Act applies (offences triable only summarily other than by virtue of express provision).</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Every enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies shall have effect as if for the specified amount less than £50 there mentioned there were substituted—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>£25 if the specified amount is less than £20; or</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>£50 if the specified amount is not less than £20.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/6" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/6" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-6"><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where, by virtue of any enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies by virtue of sub-sub-paragraph (a) of that sub-paragraph, a person convicted of a summary offence would, apart from this paragraph, be liable to a fine, or maximum fine, of one amount in the case of a first conviction and of a different amount in the case of a second or subsequent conviction, sub-paragraph (5) above shall apply separately in relation to each specified amount less than £50, even if this produces the same instead of different amounts for different convictions.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/7" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-7"><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Sub-paragraph (3) above does not apply to so much of any enactment as, in whatever words, makes a person liable or provides for a person to be made liable, on summary conviction, to a fine or a maximum fine for each period of a specified length during which a continuing offence is committed.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/8" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/8" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-8"><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies provides or confers a power to provide for, on conviction of an offence triable only summarily, a fine or a maximum fine in respect of a specified quantity or a specified number of things, “<Term id="term-the-specified-amount">the specified amount</Term>” for the purposes of subsection (5) above is the fine or maximum fine so provided or for which provision may be made.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/9" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/9" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-9"><Pnumber>9</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In sub-paragraph (3) above “<Term id="term-pre-1949-enactment">pre-1949 enactment</Term>” means an enactment passed before 1st January 1949 or an enactment passed on or after that date which whether directly or, through successive re-enactments, indirectly re-enacts with or without modification an enactment passed before that date.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/10" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/10" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-10"><Pnumber>10</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this paragraph, “<Term id="term-enactment">enactment</Term>” does not include an enactment contained in an order, regulation or and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/1/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/1/b" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-1-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>were specified in the third column of Schedule 1 to that Act.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/2" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (1) of section 15 of the 1974 Act (health and safety regulations), regulations under that section may repeal or modify any of the provisions mentioned in sub-paragraph (1) above.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/3" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Nothing in sub-paragraph (1) above shall affect the operation of section 18 of the 1974 Act (enforcement of relevant statutory provisions) in relation to any time before such day as the Secretary of State may by order made by statutory instrument appoint, and different days may be appointed for different purposes.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>
